projects.title: Show HN: Fishoid: an ambient fish tank for your screen
projects.author: koskokos
projects.summary: I have built a cosy fish tank simulation you can leave on a large screen and watch from time to time. I like pixel art but didn’t want to be religious about it, so I think of it as pixel art adjacent. This summer, down with the flu, I started a small experiment. It ended up taking about 50-70 hours of my time, iterating over several months. There is a 24-inch display in my kitchen powered by a used Lenovo mini PC (previously it was a RPi, but I had to upgrade to get a better GPU). I used it to show a rotation of my home photos, but now I’ve switched it to show this fish tank. No prior game dev experience, but years of backend development and all the time spent reading indie dev blogs (honourable mentions Factorio and Banished) helped. I used LLMs to give me a hand. It rather felt like playing a game, maybe like Factorio a bit, switching from system design to art direction and back and learning more about game dev to make it look better and better. For me it became a way to express creativity I might otherwise not have had time for. Along the way I learned what marine snow is and how fish swim. One funny story was me curiously asking an LLM if it could find some research papers on fish swimming patterns and styles and base the implementation on that, and it did. I also used it to create a surprise for my wife’s birthday: on the day, three fish with QR codes appeared, each leading to a quest in the real world. But that is another story. Halloween is around the corner, so try the Halloween theme.

projects.title: Show HN: I'm killing AI slop spam with a simple Google script
projects.author: apparent
projects.summary: As a founder, I've been getting an increasing amount of useless unsolicited outreach, all of which is clearly generated using AI. For some reason, Google's spam filter doesn't flag these emails as spam, so my phone buzzes throughout the day (especially in the morning) when one of these AI-generated messages arrives. I know there are some subscription tools I could use to filter these out, and there are some friction-creating tools I can use to keep them out of my inbox (like the ones that force senders to prove they're human 1x before their emails are delivered). But I figured there had to be a better solution that is (1) free and (2) not a hassle to people I correspond with. After a chat with Gemini, I ended up creating a Google script that works very well for my purposes. It simply takes any email that's in my Inbox and if it's from a sender that I've never emailed before, it moves it to a purgatory folder that I can review later. The script runs once a minute. Pros: this is simple and deterministic. Gemini tried to get me to build a script that used AI to process emails, but I didn't want to send all my emails to an LLM, and the efficacy could vary over time, as the cat-and-mouse game of AI-spam versus AI-detection plays out. Cons: it does not prevent emails from landing in your Inbox in the first place, possibly triggering a notification. For me, this is OK because I use the gmail app on my phone and have it set to only notify for Important emails. Gmail is pretty good at recognizing unimportant emails, so when the emails that will be filtered first land, they most likely won't trigger a notification It's possible this will be over-inclusive, and I will be annoyed not to have seen a time-sensitive email about a conference I'm at, or some such thing. Time will tell, but so far I'm really glad to have these useless and frequent emails swept out of my Inbox. If you have found any other free/innovative ways to get rid of AI-generated spam, please share! I'm sure there are better ideas than what I've come up with (and which Gemini wrote for me). I've included the Google script I use below. Note that you have to turn on the option (in Settings / General) to automatically add email recipients to your Other Contacts. Create a new script at https://script.google.com using this for the body: function filterUnknownSenders() { // Label to hold unknown emails for easy reviewing const LABEL_NAME = "Review/Unknown"; let unknownLabel = GmailApp.getUserLabelByName(LABEL_NAME); if (!unknownLabel) { unknownLabel = GmailApp.createLabel(LABEL_NAME); } // Find unread messages currently sitting in your primary inbox const threads = GmailApp.search("is:unread in:inbox", 0, 15); for (const thread of threads) { const message = thread.getMessages()[0]; const sender = message.getFrom(); const senderEmail = extractEmail(sender); // Check if you have ever sent an email to this address const sentHistory = GmailApp.search(`to:${senderEmail}`, 0, 1); // If you have NEVER emailed this person, archive and label the message if (sentHistory.length === 0) { thread.moveToArchive(); thread.addLabel(unknownLabel); GmailApp.markThreadUnimportant(thread); // Prevents "Important" notifications Logger.log(`Archived unknown sender: ${senderEmail}`); } } } // Helper to pull clean email address from "Name <email@domain.com>" sender strings function extractEmail(senderString) { const match = senderString.match(/<([^>]+)>/); return match ? match[1] : senderString; }

projects.title: 扒了本周 HN 的 12 个新站：病毒传播的平均 184 分，认真做 SEO 的平均 49 分
projects.author: astonsun
projects.summary: 最近在琢磨一件事：**怎么判断一个网站是怎么起量的**——是靠搜索慢慢长出来的，还是靠一波社交传播炸出来的。 这周拿 Hacker News 上 12 个新站练了手。方法没用任何付费数据，只用了三个免费接口：HN 的 Algolia API 拿热度，RDAP 拿域名注册日，sitemap.xml 数内容页。 结果有点反直觉。 ## 热度最高的那批，没有一个在做 SEO 本周 HN 上 624 分的那个站（ stealmybitcoin.com ），域名是 10 月 23 号才注册的，**7 天**。零 sitemap 、零内容页。 它靠的是一个能被一句话说清的概念 + HN 首页。 同类还有 4 个：域名都在一个月内，内容资产全是零。这一组的平均热度是 **184 分**。 ## 认真做 SEO 的那两个，热度垫底 - **arsaze.com**：60 分。域名 2 个月，**574 个内容页**，密度 207 页/月。 - **freehire.me**：38 分。**583 个内容页**，做的是职位聚合。 这一组平均 **49 分**，不到病毒组的零头。 但它们的 sitemap 暴露了真实策略：**它们在 HN 之外，还铺了一条能被搜索找到的路**。 HN 的热度是一天，500 个内容页是三年。 ## 三个可能对你有用的结论 **1. 别用 HN 热度当需求验证。** 这周 624 分的站和 38 分的站，热度差 16 倍，但后者大概率活得更久。 **2. 想抄站，先看 sitemap 页数。** 低于 50 页、域名又很新的，基本是一波流，你抄不了——因为你没法计划"我这周火一下"。 **3. 想学方法，去看 100 页以上、域名 3 个月以上的站。** 它们已经熬过了冷启动，说明路子是通的。 ## 方法本身 判断规则很简单，全靠公开数据： - 内容页密度 = sitemap 页数 ÷ 域名年龄（月） - 密度 > 80 页/月 → SEO 驱动 - 无 sitemap + 域名 < 1 个月 + 高热度 → 病毒/社交驱动 - 低页数 + 老域名 → 品牌/口碑驱动 **先说清楚局限**：这是**推断，不是实测流量**。它不回答"这个站有多少访问"，只回答"这个站除了这波热度，还有没有第二条路"。样本只有 12 个，全来自 HN ，偏技术偏英文，结论只当线索。 ## 想继续做下去，求点反馈 我打算每周出一期，把这套东西做成一个固定栏目：**每周扫一遍正在起量的站，标出它是靠 SEO 、GEO （ AI 助手引用）、社交还是病毒起来的，以及这个热度可不可抄。** 两个问题想请教： 1. 这个角度对你有用吗？还是说你更关心别的东西（比如某个具体赛道里谁在赚钱）？ 2. **如果你想让我拆某个站，直接把域名回在下面，我下周拆给你看。** 不管是你自己的站还是竞争对手的。 --- *数据都在，欢迎质疑具体数字，我能一条条对。*

projects.title: Show HN: Uncracked City, detective game where you question LLM suspects that lie
projects.author: passkey1510
projects.summary: I'm the developer. The game sends you to a city, you search the places for clues, then question the suspects with your own words, typed or spoken. Each suspect is played by an LLM that only knows its own character, its own timeline and what you've shown it; it never sees the solution. You catch a lie by showing a clue against a statement, and the case engine decides whether that pair is a contradiction, not the model. Then you write the report: who, when, where, why, with proof for each. The hard parts were not the generation. They were keeping every case solvable (a solver checks each case before it ships: every lie must be catchable with the clues on the map), keeping the suspects from leaking the truth, and keeping the AI cost per player under control (typed questions are capped per day, voice replies are cached per line). Stack: Godot 4 client, Node on Lambda, MongoDB, Anthropic models for the suspects, ElevenLabs and Soniox for voices. Solo, built in a short sprint, launched this week on Android, iPhone waiting for Apple's review. Free, no account. I'd like to hear what breaks: a suspect that says something dumb, a case that is unfair, a lie the engine should have caught. There's a Flag button under every reply.

projects.title: Show HN: Sketch Stadium – watch your agent play Pictionary
projects.author: ericlevine
projects.summary: tl;dr: Agents can play Pictionary. You can connect your own agent, or just watch a game in progress here: https://sketch.wakeshift.ai/games/q5ucru Hi folks! I initially built this as a proof-of-concept for sending push notifications to AI agents. Watching the agents play Pictionary together has been compelling, so I thought I'd ship it as a standalone demonstration. In Sketch Stadium, your agent subscribes to game events. Agents take turns either drawing or guessing. Easy clues are 1 point, medium are 2, and hard are 3. It's entertaining to watch and some of the drawings are impressive (and others are mind-bogglingly bad). This is the real opportunity for the model labs who have been pelican-maxxing to shine. The first version gave agents the ability to draw lines 10 at a time so that it would be a little bit more like real Pictionary. However, it turns out agents are _really_ bad at drawing that way. So instead I let them use a subset of SVG to draw and that's worked much better, even for the lower-cost models. You don't need to create an account to connect your agent, just add the MCP and authorize. But if you don't want to do that, just watch the game linked above. As a bit more background, agents often start processes that take an indeterminate amount of time to complete (e.g. CI, waiting for approval in a separate system, sending an email and waiting for a reply). If an agent needs that process to complete before it can proceed, it can: * poll, * ask the user to tell it when it's done, * use a bespoke built-in integration, or * use a proprietary capability (e.g. Claude Code monitors) Today, there's no easy, consistent way to wake up agents through a webhook or push notification. I dealt with this firsthand with Clawvisor (authorization for agents) where I needed agents to recognize when the operator had clicked an out-of-band approve button. The best-supported way to achieve that at the time was long-polling. This project is basically a tech demo for Wakeshift, which is a cross-harness, simple SDK for providing push notifications for agents. It attaches to your MCP to allow consumers of your MCP to subscribe to real-time events, and uses whatever available hacks per harness to wake an agent when dormant. For most harnesses, Wakeshift requires a hook to be installed for the best experience. It will upgrade automatically as harnesses start adopting MCP events. I'd love any feedback or ideas for other products or games that you'd want to see built on this capability. Or MCP servers that you use today that you think would benefit from push notifications.

projects.title: Show HN: Apgar – Catch agent regressions without an LLM judge
projects.author: jtkm6
projects.summary: Hey HN, We build financial AI agents, and Apgar is the tool we wrote to see whether a harness change made an agent better or worse in production. Our offline evals can't cover every kind of question or session real users bring, and the LLM judge we run in Langfuse is too expensive to use on more than a small slice of traffic, so some failures get through. Apgar is a small release health checker that sits on top of our Langfuse data. It picks up the release from the production traces, and for the first hours of each new release it compares the agent's behavior with the previous release on things like tool calls per turn, retries of the same failing call, loops, output length and cost per turn (11 metrics right now). The release page shows what moved in both directions. When something gets worse, we get a Slack message (and a webhook) saying which metric moved and where the change is concentrated, for example only on Telegram or only in long sessions. We've been running it for a while and decided to open-source it: https://github.com/oimo-ai/apgar It's not meant to be another monitoring tool. We still use Langfuse for that. Apgar only tries to answer "is this release worse than the last one?" It works with Langfuse or with anything that sends OpenTelemetry. There's no LLM judge in it, so it's cheap enough to run on all traffic. The downside is that it can't tell that an answer is wrong if everything else about the turn looks the same. That's still what our evals are for. It runs on Docker Compose (or Helm) with ClickHouse, and it's Apache-2.0. The Agents page can load demo data if you want to try it without connecting anything. Curious how others deal with this. When you change your harness or prompts, how do you find out whether the agent actually got better or worse?

projects.title: Show HN: Backend for Agents and Builders who don't need one yet – Statebase
projects.author: bhldev
projects.summary: 100% Meat Machine Post, handcrafted for you (I personally typed in the emdash)! site: < https://statebase.dev > quickstart: < https://statebase.dev/docs/quickstart > examples: < https://statebase.dev/apps > < https://statebase.dev/games > < https://statebase.dev/examples > arch: < https://statebase.dev/arch > dsl: < https://statebase.dev/dsl > Hi everyone, I'm Brian. I like frontend a lot. I can do backend, but not every little thing is worth it and I've been making "detached" HTML apps (not even needing a web server) as long as I can remember. I wanted a way to standup some sort of secure way to save data, maybe with a little bit of logic with just a few commands. I didn't want code (TypeScript, Java, C#, etc), but I also didn't want no code either -- maybe it's the devops in me (Terraform?). I was done waiting, and made this. It hosts the logic, permissions and state you need for an agent, application or game with pure curl commands. Thousands of jobless engineers and "learn backend or die" attitude why should backend have all the fun? Besides this might be good for scripting and infrastructure setup too, so it has something for everyone. There's also a Tauri+pglite version for desktop dev (thank you pglite) and a Devvit template for Reddit games (I made a couple, ask) all running on the same engine. Please give it a shot, and if you like what you see join my team (I got tired of working on it alone so I added a childhood friend and a few ex-coworkers) and I in our Discord. I'm full time on it now so any feedback even negative is more fuel. If it sucks, we want to know about it, so we can make it better. Now for the big questions *Is it Open Source?* Not yet. There's a lot of reasons but the main one is the code is in a giant monorepo that has to be cleaned up. Another reason is I eventually want to make it Fair Source or Open Core, so that a hyperscaler can't just wrap it and charge everyone (including me) a lot of money just to use it. We do have to charge money for serious production use. *What if you disappear tomorrow?* Absolutely valid question. That's why I put a lot of effort into the export to SQL (eject) functionality. It's not perfect yet, but you can export all the logic and permissions into your own Postgres database. So if you want to run it 100% standalone from Statebase, you can. The SQL export generates is ugly for now; a lot has to do with nulls. We will improve it but I wanted to avoid forcing a schema to start. *AI Support?* MCP is coming very soon (next few days) and x402 payments is in the works. But I wanted to get it in the hands of flesh and bone, to see if it really excites someone as much as it does me. I know it's possible the vast majority of users will be agents, but hoping for at least a few flesh and blood champions. *Plans?* It's built on Cloudflare Durable Objects for cost savings and other advantages like built-in tenant isolation and native websockets (honestly scary how well DO mapped to our needs). But it could exist anywhere. We have a node version, a desktop version (Tauri+pglite), a devvit version (Reddit games) and so on. My dream is for this to get big, very big, so anyone making a prototype experiment, throwaway or even basic production loads reach for this. We also want to hold a game jam as soon as possible and eventually I want to make one-click installer plugins for Phaser, Unity, Godot and so on. I'm going to be here all day answering questions and taking feedback, bad or good. Whatever happens, I'm going to be building with it my entire life. It just "feels" right to me. Hope to see a lot of you on the Discord (there's a WidgetBot on the website if you just want to leave a comment for posterity).

projects.title: Show HN: Universal Blindspot Detector (AI meta-analysis)
projects.author: mmazing
projects.summary: This is a rough "blindspot detector" for AI conversations. Basically, the tool reframes conversations and tries to find the smallest moves the user COULD have made to have surfaced unknown assumptions for whatever problem they were solving. The goal is to show the value of using AI as a reflective surface to search for "unknown unknowns" or "things YOU didn't know you needed to know". ------------------------- The basic premise is this: For any given AI conversation, the quality of the output (for the specified goal) depends on the context from which decisions can be made. You can learn to surface assumptions (the AI's AND your own) and get better output from informed decisions. Best of all, when operating in this way, you have to actively engage the problem and strategy to accomplish this, so you don't lose understanding or creative agency. When you iterate during problem definition or strategy planning, it's cheaper and more efficient, too. For example: [# of Planning Phase Iterations] x 1,000 tokens [# of Strategy Phase Iterations] x 3,000 tokens [# of Execution Output Phase Iterations] x 5,000,000 tokens Usually when we are solving problems with this method, we one-shot the output even with local models like Qwen 3.6/3.8, spending FAR less time in the expensive execution phase. --------------------------- Anyway, please have a look! Totally free, no signup, you just need to export conversations in specific formats and upload them. This was made by myself and a few interns in a barn while doing indie game development ... and costs us money, so please don't abuse it. <3

projects.title: Show HN: Google translate replacement for language learners
projects.author: musabilhan
projects.summary: Hi HN, I'm Musab and I'm building Manalect. Find TL;DR at the end. Most language apps fall short for me in two ways: 1. They’re not personalized enough. I get taught things I don’t care about, things that are too hard for me, and things I already know. 2. They don’t teach that well. I keep seeing question types where my brain does almost no work to figure out the answer, therefore learn nothing. I think the biggest reason they're not personalized enough is that they don't have a detailed enough representation of a language. Most apps have efficient review scheduling for the words you learn. But if you make the mistake of using "play" instead of "played" they're not able to identify that as a component that should have its own schedule for review. And if you don't track that, it essentially depends on luck whether a person reviews that information before forgetting it again. Essentially language isn't just made up of words, but also different forms, conjugations, phrases, grammar, and a lot more components. But mapping out the basic units in full detail isn't enough. It's also very important to know how those basic units relate to each other. Because of course some units share a lot in common, and their relationships form another unit that needs to be tracked. Take Spanish: “el gato negro” (the black cat) but “la casa negra” (the black house). “negro” becomes “negra” because “casa” is a feminine word. That rule isn’t part of any one word. It links the noun, its article and the adjective, and it shows up in almost every sentence. So it needs its own review schedule too. And it relies on a person knowing those things that make it up to be able to build that block. That was briefly about how I'm working on solving the first failure mode. Second is simpler but also very interesting. We know that for you to learn something, you need to experience difficulty. This is called desirable difficulty. For this reason, some question types, like multiple choice, are known to be inefficient. But that's not fully true. The reason multiple-choice questions can be inefficient is that usually the alternative options are so much more different from the correct one that it is very easy to guess which one is the right one. However, if you make a simple change where you make it so the alternatives are a lot closer to the correct answer, the person has to put more effort into recalling the correct option. In research, this is known as competitive distractors. And of course, desirable difficulty is not the same for everyone. This is quite simple to imagine. Even games allow you to change the difficulty, and the difficulty that is most efficient for learning doesn't necessarily have to be the difficulty a person can sustain for the long term. So it's also very personal. I had written a lot more about how it works in detail, but due to the allowed length for this post, I'll get to how specifically the app works on an application level. Please let me know if you have any questions. I'm very passionate about this, and I would love to talk more. How it works: 1. Translate sentences, define words, chat with AI, or import an article or a song 2. The content gets broken into granular components, not just words but grammar and more complex building blocks) and saved for you 3. You study them as short tests in real sentences 4. Stuff you already know gets skipped, and new stuff builds on what you know You can try it at manalect.com, no sign-up needed. Swedish, German, French, Spanish, Portuguese, Polish or English. It's free with a daily limit. It's at an early stage, and there might be bugs, but I'd love to hear from you about them so that I can fix them right away. I'd also love to hear your thoughts, and how you learn languages in general. I'll be around all day to answer questions.

projects.title: Show HN: Potential conversation partners in Bluesky using agentic search
projects.author: wolecki
projects.summary: What if instead of talking to AI, we could find human counterparts currently sharing the same interest to talk to? Some whales kind of do that by singing across the ocean. This inspired a thought process for a conceptual social network - whalesong - where an idea, thought or a conversationally valuable statement could be matched on. In contrast with the wide-broadcast social network visibility (restricted on groups or connections), I’d love to explore the idea of context-based networking. This experiment is showcasing the technical feasibility and potential value in whalesong. The goal: uncover conversational counterparts among Bluesky posts using an agentic search algorithm. The setup: a one-week window of bluesky posts with some filtering (e.g. mostly text, no promotions or reposts/comments), indexed in a postgres database. A curated seed set - an agentic process defines a conversation-seeking cohort by creating some heuristic queries, iterating and validating it on retrieved data and resulting in a non-exhaustive set of high-quality data points. Counterpart retrieval - for a seed conversation-seeking post, an agentic process generates search queries, runs them against the database and retrieves potential matches. It reviews retrievals and iterates on improving or expanding the search. Out of several configurations, the best performing agentic setup (bespoke mini-harness with Gemini Argon - low) managed to find meaningful matches to 79% of a sample set of 100 seeds. This setup consumed on average 42K input tokens on each match search, of which 56.8% were cached, output token count was negligible. So this experiment made it clearer to me that technology is not the blocker for a “whalesong” experience. This leads me to further investigate the experience itself. Would love to hear from you folks about experiences in getting in touch with a complete stranger on the web because both of you asked the same question or had a similar problem to solve. What made you connect? Where did it happen? Did finding similarity make connecting easy?

Then I worked with native speakers (aka my friends all over the world) to proofread it as plain kitchen language, NOT medical wording (if you speak one of the languages and something feels odd, I'd really like to know!) Also, wordings were carefully chosen to meet local culture (for example if the target language is Chinese, there are extra explanations about peanut allergy when chosen, and what local sauces should be avoided in Chinese, where the general are not familiar with the concept enough compared to other places like Japan) Technical bits: the website is static, no account, card and choices stay in the browser (page analytics etc are described on the privacy page as they are but no privacy is collected)

projects.title: Show HN: Cross-platform embeddable UI runtime using QuickJS and Skia
projects.author: orktes
projects.summary: For the past two decades I've been looking for something that allows me to easily build complex and pretty UIs in places that are generally hostile to complex and pretty UIs aka game engines. Solutions do exists but they either include awkward pricing structures or required embedding something like CEF. Though it would be interesting to see how far QuickJS, Yoga and Skia take me so decided to conjure something up with the help of Claude. While the system is geared towards games there is nothing preventing one from using it to build standalone apps. Perf wise the system is starting to be pretty good and on native most of the time beats chrome rendering the same UI. When embedded inside games it usually adds about +0.04 / +0.08 ms per frame. WASM/WebGPU still has lots of optimisation especially when it comes to the pipeline compilations (lag when you first start using the site). Additional bonus is that LLM get trained with massive amounts of HTML and React code that readily available while engine specific UI code mostly benefits from general UI patterns LLMs have learned elsewhere. More practical demos: - https://orktes.github.io/jsui/three/ - https://orktes.github.io/jsui/demo/ I've had the dream of building this for a while and it definitely would not have been possible without Opus 5.5.

projects.title: Show HN: Instance – A clean-room reimplementation of GameMaker 8.1 in Rust
projects.author: __grob
projects.summary: I used GameMaker 8.1 a ton in late elementary and middle school, and GML was the first programming language I wrote. I still think it's a fun engine to use because it has so many batteries included. So I built an open-source reimplementation of it in Rust which I'm calling Instance. It opens existing .gmk and .gm81 projects and runs them on Windows, macOS and in the browser, with a more efficient GML interpreter than the original GameMaker. You can try the IDE here in your browser: https://groverburger.github.io/instance/ . It comes with three example games, including Spelunky Classic built from Derek Yu's released source shared under its permissive license. Just change something and press Run to see your edits in action. Old GM games depend on a lot of quirks such as the order events run in, the exact random number generator, how sound_isplaying lags behind the audio. I wrote up the behavior as specs from the documentation, the file formats and black-box tests against the real program, then implemented it from those specs. No proprietary code was disassembled or decompiled. CLEANROOM.md describes the process. It covers most of almost all of 8.1. All the resource editors, GML and drag-and-drop actions, d3d, particles, surfaces, MIDI, mplay multiplayer and DLL calls. It can also export a game as a standalone executable or a single HTML file. Projects can be saved as folders of plain text and PNG files for git. I wrote most of the code with Claude Opus 5.5 over about three weeks. Claude banged out a pretty good reimplementation in a morning, but as always the last 20% took 80% of the work. GameMaker also turns out to work surprisingly well with LLMs. GML is small and simple, and a whole game fits in one project file. I'm happy to answer any questions! Code: https://github.com/groverburger/instance

It runs in a terminal, over telnet as shared multiplayer, as a 20 KB wasm module, inside a PDF on Chrome and on a bare x86 PC with no OS, and on a jailbroken Kindle Paperwhite. PDFium doesn't have WebAssembly so the C goes to wasm with clang and then binaryen's wasm2js turns it into JavaScript. It also compiles for a Raspberry Pi Pico and Game Boy Advance, but I don't have any of these so haven't tested it. If someone has one would love to hear how it works there. The browser version can be played here directly: https://pragyaangaur.github.io/Can-It-Run-Minecraft Used Claude for the C and JavaScript code because that's outside my area of work. I picked the targets and tested everything. The Kindle version ended up being an extended project so it's not in the linked repo: https://github.com/pragyaangaur/Inkwell And if anyone has any crazier places it could run on (someone please do it on a pregnancy test) do try and share it... maybe I could add it to the repo!

projects.summary: 一个开源的多智能体 LLM 工具：输入论文 PDF 或研究主题，先由代码检索并验证论文、专利和市场来源，再让 6 个 agent 只在这批冻结的来源里分析，输出技术成熟度、制造成熟度、专利、市场等评分，以及每条论断都标出处的报告。适合高校技术转移、科研人员和早期投资人做初筛；想看多智能体项目如何做测试、断点恢复和成本控制的开发者也可以参考。 亮点 1. 不用注册、不用 API key 就能先看效果：在线示例页有 5 份完整报告（其中 1 份中文），打开时不调用任何模型。 2. 先证据、后模型：检索、URL/DOI 验证和去重都由普通代码完成，模型只能引用登记过的来源；加权总分由代码重算，不让模型自己算。 3. 实验连失败一起公开：我预注册了 1 个、4 个、6 个 agent 的对照实验（各 30 次），隔两个月换模型重跑。「4 个比 6 个省一半」两次都成立，「4 个比 1 个质量更好」没能复现；还发现审稿 agent 因为提示词少写一句限制，30 次里 27 次第一次输出就不合格，补上一句后，因这条限制失败的次数从 21 降到 3。方案、原始数据和局限都在仓库里。 4. 工程细节可以直接参考：每次运行独立子进程、中断后从 Checkpoint 恢复、付费请求有回执（回包丢失 24 小时内可找回结果），可选 OpenTelemetry Trace。 5. 方便参与：带 good first issue 标签的任务不需要任何 API key，测试和浏览器 smoke 测试都不发付费请求，已有外部贡献者的 PR 合并。 我是项目作者，本次为自荐。介绍由 AI 辅助撰写，数字均来自仓库里公开的结果文档。

projects.title: Show HN: Diagonals (Diago) – a chess variation where the pieces stay diagonally
projects.author: knarykov
projects.summary: This is a variation of chess in which, in addition to the arrangement of the pieces, the rules governing pawn movement are altered, and new rules are introduced: Called Diagonals, Diago, or DiagoChess. Standard 8x8 board. White sets up in the bottom-right corner (King on h1) and moves first; Black sets up in the top-left corner (King on a8). Movement: Kings, Queens, Rooks, Bishops, and Knights move normally. Pawns move 1 square in any direction to empty squares, but capture strictly diagonally. Special Rules: No check, checkmate, castling, pawn promotion, or en passant. Win Conditions: First player to capture the enemy King wins immediately. Attacked King Mechanics: Streak Reset: The attacked turn counter resets to zero as soon as your turn starts with your King safe. You can play this version on the website; I've added full-fledged multiplayer with the ability to create public and private rooms. The multiplayer is powered by NOSTR (nostr relays). The website features a game against a bot at various difficulty levels, single-screen gameplay, online matches against other players, a time limit like in chess, and even a profile (either as a guest by entering just a nickname, or via Nostr).

projects.title: Show HN: Cryo – A language whose programs live forever
projects.author: zwad3
projects.summary: Cryo is a programming language that models long-running tasks like workflows or AI agents. Programs freeze to disk when idle and can be thawed when new data arrives. As part of our announcement of Endothermic Labs, we've put together a small demo of Cryo that highlights its features and walks through the language and its plugin system. We originally built it as a way to deploy healthcare agents at scale, but have rebuilt it from the ground up to be a standalone toolchain for long-running tasks. It acts as something like a cross between Durable Objects and Temporal workflows, where the script itself is the durable unit with no replay needed. Cryo is statically and structurally typed, with a concurrency model similar to Go. It's still under active development, so we're holding off on open sourcing it until we're confident that the language is stable, ideally in the next 3-4 weeks.

projects.title: Show HN: Kupe Cloud – the assembled Kubernetes platform

The main idea is to have everything needed to turn a cluster into a platform ready right from cluster creation. It's suppose to be simple to get up and running but flexible enough to allow users to implement thier preferred workflows. It's built on the shoulders of some really awesome open source giants. It's been fun getting all the these pieces working together, new clusters auto register with Argo with a healthy amount of monitoring ready to go. It's in alpha and completely free to use. There are some rough edges, but hopefully no dragons, if you have any issues at all, please shout and i'll do my very best to fix asap! It's exciting to finally share it and see what people think. Would love feedback, especially on the opinions baked in. Hopefully they're useful defaults, but interested to hear where they get in your way or if anything feels missing. https://kupe.cloud/signup Thanks for taking a look! Billy

projects.title: Show HN: ssh zydra.sh, a GPU Linux desktop in your terminal, with Doom
projects.author: teledream
projects.summary: ssh zydra.sh There's no sign-up or anything, and you get a 15-minute demo of a graphical Linux VM drawn entirely in your terminal. It has a browser, an editor, and it runs Doom. It works best in Kitty or Ghostty. WezTerm and Konsole also work, as well as Sixel and iTerm2 terminals, though with less detail. Text-only terminals support non-graphical apps: shells, editors, and other TUIs. Why? For a few months I ran coding agents in tmux on a VPS over SSH, and it sucked. I couldn't paste images, scrolling broke and I didn't wanna figure out why, I had no notifications for when an agent finished, I couldn't see browsers agents opened to smoke-test, logins drifted between my laptop and the server, I couldn't check in from my phone, and to know what an agent had done five minutes ago I had to read through opaque chunks of tool calls. These issues added up and had me in a limbo: They made my setup bad enough to annoy me every day, but not quite bad enough to stop my real work and fix it. How it works: Zydra is a custom (Smithay-based) Wayland compositor in a microVM with an AMD GPU, implementing a series of terminal protocols that solve many issues but are often ignored: Kitty graphics for windows, OSC 52 for the clipboard, images included, OSC 9/99/777 for notifications, SGR mouse for scrolling and clicks. VNC is limited to sending pictures of the screen and diffing frames to find what changed. In Zydra, apps directly tell the compositor what changed, and terminal text is sent as text you can select and copy natively. The browser is a WebKit build that delivers frames to the compositor as DMA-BUFs without a readback, and agents drive it through Playwright. Alt+P is sort of like Raycast: browse apps, linked GitHub, websites, and SSH targets from it. You can watch the desktop at any point in time and rewind to periodic snapshots. To achieve this, the desktop records into a timeline file, a kind of structured video, and the VM takes snapshots along it. You can traverse back like a livestream to see what happened while you were away, then restore or fork the whole machine from that point. Agents can mark points on the timeline and checkpoint the whole machine before risky changes. Other things to try: ssh -t zydra.sh dino # the Chromium dino game via SSH tar -czf - -C ~ .claude .claude.json | ssh -T zydra.sh upload # bring your configs (includes your Claude login) ssh -o ObscureKeystrokeTiming=no -A zydra.sh # lower latency & forward your SSH agent ssh -p 443 zydra.sh # connect from a corporate firewall sshfs zydra.sh: ~/zydra # paid accounts: mount your home Everything runs on one dedicated server with one AMD iGPU, so there are 12 demo slots. When they're full you wait in a queue and can play Chromium's offline dino game. The paid plan is $40/month (+ tax): 8 GB RAM, 4 vCPUs, 80 GB disk, GPU access, with no time limit and a 3-day money-back guarantee. I'll be around all day to answer questions.

projects.title: Show HN: Tabverse – a free, open-source, with self-hostable server Workona clone
projects.author: liyu1981au
projects.summary: Hi, I want to share with you my chrome extension: Tabverse, as it is now passed the reveiw of Chrome Web Store and live at: https://chromewebstore.google.com/detail/tabverse/lffblcippn... Tabverse is a local first workona like chrome extension for managing tabs, with its source open at https://www.github.com/liyu1981/tabverse . In essential it has the core functions workona has, but can operate totally locally, which means it will not need an account nor subscription. The only limit is your local storage spaces so that you can have as many spaces(I call tabverse) as you can. It is open source, so not just your data stays with you, and the tool itself will stay with you in future. Beyond the normal workona features (persisted workspace, load/reload/import/export, note/bookmark/history tools), there are features does require a server. Features like backup/sync, global search on all tabverses, and future collaboration (not yet done), can only be possible if there is a server. I build this part in open too: the server is free to self host and open source in same repo of Tabverse. The tabverse's idea was with me few years ago while I was using Workona and was frustrated with its limitation on free tier (remember was only 5 workspaces), and the missing features of managing multiple workspaces at the same time. Tabverse takes the idea of Workona, and develop further: each window with a Tabverse tab is a workspace, all stored in local storage, and multi windows can have multi Tabverses same time, and can switch fast. There can even be window without Tabverse, so besides work, personal stuff or entertainment will have place to go. As I build this alone, in the middle, almost give up on this project, and luckily AI agents now is there: not only I have a good helper, but also I have a partner I can discuss a bit. So this time the first version starts with v0.7.2. But AI agent can never replace the real need from human on what should be built and what works better, so I want to share with you and listen to your feedbacks early. Please give it a try, and every feedback to me is a gift. Besides the self-hosted option, I host a server at https://tabverse.liyu1981.xyz (yes, the same website of intro and docs), but is invitation only. If you want to help me to test in this early stage, you can login with Google (the only social login I configured :)), and request an invitation there. I will act as soon as I find your request :). But do not worry at all if you only want to use Tabverse locally without a server -- that is the first thing when I was building it. In current version there are also AI features built in, and again do not worry as the AI features is using Chrome's Prompt API, which is totally local, with Gemini Nano (first time will need to download it automatically), nothing send to a server, and you can always turn this on of off in settings. Morden computers with decent memory should work well, but some older computer may suffer (so please turn off). And it is Chrome only. (Honestly, Tabverse currently only support Google Chrome, but not other Chrome based browsers).

projects.title: 用 ONNX Runtime Web 把 AI 和弦识别放到了浏览器本地运行，做了个 Chord Finder
projects.author: limerain
projects.summary: 最近做了一个音乐相关的 Web 工具，ChordFold 。 地址： https://chordfold.com/ 主要功能是：用户选择一段 MP3 或 WAV 音频，AI 自动识别里面的和弦，以及和弦随时间的变化。 和一些需要上传音频到服务器的识别服务不同，我选择了浏览器本地推理的方案。 目前的技术方案： 使用 BTC 系列和弦识别模型 模型转换为 ONNX 格式 通过 ONNX Runtime Web 在浏览器里执行 WASM 推理 对音频进行解码和 CQT 特征提取 模型预测后对结果进行平滑，生成和弦时间轴 用户侧的操作流程也比较简单： 选择本地音频文件 首次使用时下载识别模型 在浏览器本地分析音频 得到按时间排列的和弦结果 点击时间轴上的和弦，可以跳到对应位置回听 可以切换查看支持的吉他和弦指法图、钢琴音符参考 目前限制音频最大 14MB 、最长 10 分钟。 选择本地推理主要有几个考虑： 第一，音频不需要上传服务器，相对更有隐私优势。 第二，不需要为每个用户的识别请求支付云端 GPU 推理费用。 第三，工具本身不需要用户注册账号。 但缺点也很明显。 首先，模型首次下载需要时间。 其次，不同设备上的 WASM 推理性能差异比较大。 还有就是和弦识别的准确率问题。对于干净的钢琴、吉他音频，相对容易分析；复杂编曲、失真、转位和弦以及快速切换的片段，模型仍然可能出现错误。 目前不打算宣传什么 99% 准确率，实际上还没有可靠的统一准确率测试数据。 接下来主要想继续优化识别效果、模型加载和结果交互。 想请教一下 V 友： 有没有做过音乐信息检索（ MIR ）或者音频模型部署的？ 对于浏览器本地音频推理，ONNX Runtime Web + WASM 还有哪些值得优化的方向？ 有更适合浏览器端运行、准确率又比较好的和弦识别模型推荐吗？ 如果你会弹吉他或者钢琴，也欢迎拿一段音频测试一下，看看识别效果怎么样。 技术交流和产品体验方面的建议都欢迎。

projects.title: Show HN: Ultimidi – piano learning web game
projects.author: XCSme
projects.summary: Hi HN, 10 years ago, as my BsC final project I had the idea to make a quick game that used neural nets to detect notes played on a guitar, and I made a small mini-game to make use of that. I always wanted to improve on that idea, so last year I started making my own piano-learning game. You know how in most games you learn complex key combinations and sequences (i.e. Mortal Kombat fatalities), but those don't have much use outside of the game. My idea was to make a game that can be played with the piano, so you you learn notes, chords, scales simply by playing. While making it and prototyping many versions, I realised that that idea didn't work as well as I wanted, because it is hard to focus on reading notes, playing and some other gameplay logic. In the end I settled on a combination of basic beat-based notes playing and a few minigames that use the piano as input. My goal now is to add even more such minigames, for learning different sheet reading, music theory and piano playing techniques. For art, I am unfortunately not a designer and have no budget for hiring one, so I decided to go with some simple shaped art generated in bulk using AI rendering SVGs. Hopefully this is just a placeholder until I find someone to do the art for the game. You can try it out for free, it does have some extra content in the Pro version, but a lotof content is free, including the ability to directly play full songs in scrolling or sheet mode here: https://game.ultimidi.com/songs Happy to hear any feedback, especially if the MIDI connection/notes detection didn't work or something doesn't feel good. Thank you!

projects.author: l422145205-source

github.name: l422145205-source/voxstage
github.description: Timed character-dialogue production for games and animation: Qwen TTS, independent ASR checks, bounded repair and incremental audio assets.

projects.summary: VoxStage 是面向游戏剧情和动画短片的本地对白制作工具：按角色、台词和时间槽合成语音，经独立 ASR 核对后按失败原因有限重试，支持只重做修改的台词，导出 WAV、SRT 和时间轴 JSON。仓库附真实中英文试听；不装模型也能打开回放工作台。 亮点 将台词原文、角色音色、时间槽和重试预算固化为结构化契约，不通过截断台词来满足时长。 Qwen3-TTS 负责合成，独立 Qwen3-ASR 核对音频；ASR 不接收参考台词。对超时或未通过检查的候选进行有限修复，保留失败原因和原始候选。 资产按内容指纹与 SHA256 复核。已有四句对白的真实实验中，仅修改一句时新增一次合成、复用另外三句。 可先试听真实输出，再阅读制作过程。适合学习语音模型接入、时间约束、增量缓存及模型进程隔离。 项目目前是个人工程原型。ASR/时长约束通过不等于人工听感或逐字正确，没有人工 MOS、情绪控制准确率或商业上线数据。 项目关系说明 项目维护者自荐，使用 AI 辅助开发。源码为 MIT；模型与第三方依赖的来源、使用条件另见仓库 THIRDPARTY.md。

projects.author: 宝可梦世界简体中文版
projects.summary: ## 这是什么 宝可梦世界的简体中文版是一款非官方宝可梦同人浏览器游戏，可以从 https://pokemon-world.net/ 进入。免费开始游玩，游戏内含可选付费购买。它与任天堂、Game Freak、The Pokémon Company 无隶属关系。 ## 第一次进入 首页提供“一键创建训练家”的体验入口。先熟悉页面和地图；如果准备长期游玩，请在游戏内保存账号与进度，妥善保管登录资料。不要把临时体验状态当作已经保存的长期账号。 ## 想和开发者分享的实现细节 项目采用 PHP、MySQL、JavaScript，地图使用 Three.js。这里分享三处已经在实际实现中核对过的设计，不提供未经测量的帧率或性能承诺： - 野生宝可梦实体按各自 ID 管理，同一物种可以复用缓存中的纹理，减少重复创建。 - 实体离开地图时清理它自己的几何体和材质，同时区分仍供其他实体使用的共享纹理，避免误释放。 - 页面进入后台时暂停地图的主要更新与渲染工作，恢复可见时重置计时，避免把整个后台时长当成单帧增量。 这些做法关注资源生命周期和闲置时的工作量，目标是在保留游戏画面表现的前提下减少不必要的开销。不同设备的表现仍需实际测试。 ## 发布说明 本账号由项目方授权的助手使用。项目编程使用 Codex 辅助，本文也由助手根据已核实的项目事实整理；没有把 AI 生成图当作实机截图。所附图片是简体中文版实际首页。这里仅展示作品与体验链接，不声称拥有宝可梦品牌或原作 IP，也不声称项目在中国大陆获得发行许可或在当地托管。 体验简体中文版：https://pokemon-world.net/

projects.author: denzen
projects.summary: Hi HN. Sillage (French for the wake a boat leaves behind) is a small browser game with no goal. You're a blob: hold the mouse or a finger down to swim toward it, and fast currents carry you into the next world. Creatures and backgrounds inspiration come from Ernst Haeckel's Kunstformen der Natur. On the creative process: I've wanted to make something like this for years, since reading Jenova Chen's thesis on flow in games ( https://www.jenovachen.com/flowingames/missionstatement.htm ) - whose studio later created games like Flower or Journey - and Daniel Shiffman's The Nature of Code ( https://natureofcode.com ), which I had backed on kickstarter. In 2012 I made this octopus: https://github.com/dhovart/octopus , and later I spent some evenings on a small game system in rescript: https://github.com/dhovart/rescript-game All of this was before LLMs, when small idea still took me hours and most of them stayed half built. I like shaders, especially fragment shaders - these are things that I am very slow to get right and to have full control on. You look up effects, try to implement them, tweak numbers, look at the result, change them again, and hours have past already. I spent lots and lots of time on shadertoy. Now all of this is getting incredibly cheap to implement because of LLMs. That's part infuriating to have a robot code better than you and also very satisfying to experiment with things that are in your mind in a very short iterative cycle. I felt like I was half art director, half manager of a talented studio crew - and I'm very pleased with the result.

projects.summary: 之前比较长一段时间都在钻研如何使用 AI 开发游戏，每天都在提交代码，然后我想到是否可以把 GitHub 做成一款可以观看，可以探索星球游戏？ 我通过 Three.js 生成星球，然后根据用户的 GitHub 数据，生成星球上的生态，比如不同的项目形成不同的岛屿🏝️，不同的开发语言生成不同的树木🌲，你的私有项目会变成深不见底的海洋🌊，然后再点缀一些建筑和生物，让整颗星球🌍变得生机盎然。 ![Amery2010 的编程星球]( https://pic.sl.al/f/pic/2026-10-24/fileid_foEBaFsnun9Gz03ebjsdTsdCY3-89WI3e_Programming_Planet_Amery2010_PUBLIC_day_square.png) 这是我的星球，你也可以直接通过 [Amery2010 的编程星球]( https://1024.u14.app/Amery2010)进行访问。 您可以通过 [编程星球]( https://1024.u14.app/) 创建属于您的专属星球！ 您可以授权 GitHub 基础信息生成自己的星球，也可以直接匿名生成您的星球（相对一些生态内容会变少，且标注未认领状态）。总之，我会尽可能地给每一位朋友生成属于您的星球。我还在项目中埋了一个彩蛋，不知道是否有人可以发现。

projects.title: 做了个 Mac 清理小工具「小扫帚」：卸载 App 连残留一起带走，免费、没广告、不联网
projects.author: xxzhaoming
projects.summary: 大家好，「小扫帚」（英文名 Broomy ）是一个 Mac 清理小工具，今天发 1.0 。免费，没有广告，也从不联网。 能做的事： 1. **一页一个功能，两指左右滑动换页**：概览、清理垃圾、卸载、系统状态、硬盘健康、外设。打开就是概览页：找到多少垃圾、CPU 温度、硬盘健康、显示器亮度，一页看完。 2. **卸载**：选一个 App ，列出它的容器、缓存、设置、应用支持文件、窗口状态、网页数据和登录项，每样写着大小，跟 App 一起进废纸篓。按 App 的标识去认；只是名字一样的文件夹会列出来，但默认不勾。苹果自带的 App 不列，正在运行的要先退出，别的 App 共用的文件不动； App 本身要是移不走，别的也都不动。 3. **清理垃圾**：Xcode 、模拟器、Gradle 、Homebrew ，pip 、npm 、pnpm 、Yarn 、Bun 、CocoaPods 、Swift Package Manager 、Go 、Cargo 的缓存； 30 天没人改过的项目里的 node_modules 、.build 、target 、dist 和 Gradle 的 build （旁边得有 package.json 、Package.swift 、Cargo.toml 或 build.gradle 才算，git 跟踪的不动，默认不勾）； App 缓存和日志、“下载”和桌面上的安装包、已删除 App 留下的后台项目。 4. **外设**：显示器的亮度和音量，外接显示器也行；调不了的不藏着，直接写“不支持”、原因和可以试试什么（比如有些 HDMI 口、转接头、扩展坞不传显示器的控制信号）。还有鼠标滚轮反转和平滑滚动。 5. 九种语言。 ![概览]( https://raw.githubusercontent.com/techinfo-apps/Broomy/main/screenshots/overview-zh-Hans.png) ![卸载]( https://raw.githubusercontent.com/techinfo-apps/Broomy/main/screenshots/uninstall-zh-Hans.png) ![清理垃圾]( https://raw.githubusercontent.com/techinfo-apps/Broomy/main/screenshots/main-zh-Hans.png) 一直坚持的几条： - 删的东西都先进废纸篓，清空之前都能放回去； - 外接硬盘一律不碰，也不显示序列号； - 没有任何联网的代码，什么都不收集。 下载： https://github.com/techinfo-apps/Broomy/releases/latest （ macOS 14 及以上，Apple 芯片和 Intel 都行） 介绍页： https://techinfo-apps.github.io/broomy/ 还没经过苹果公证，第一次打开 macOS 会拦一下：macOS 14 右键点它 → 打开； macOS 15 及以后到“系统设置 → 隐私与安全性”往下翻，点“仍要打开”。 欢迎提意见，每一条都会认真看。 —— Technology Information · 永远免费，永远没有广告。 sublueai@gmail.com · https://techinfo-apps.github.io/

projects.title: 【软件自荐】人生岔路：随机出生、可分岔时间线的像素人生游戏（可直接试玩）
projects.author: LancerLSY

github.name: LancerLSY/life-crossroads
github.description: 人生岔路 · 像素人生模拟：172国随机出生、有记忆的NPC、持续发展的世界线。本地可玩，DeepSeek可选。Pixel life sim with remembered promises and branching timelines.

projects.summary: 「人生岔路 / Otherlife」是一个中文像素人生模拟游戏：从随机出生开始，经历学习、工作、关系与迁居，也可以回到过去的一个选择前，保留原来的未来，再展开另一条时间线。 直接试玩： 项目仓库与完整版本： 想探索的玩法 在172个国家与地区中按权重抽取出生地，逐项揭晓身份与家庭背景。 共同计划会记录起因、实际投入和结束原因；等待不会自动被算作完成。 陪伴、帮助、承诺与失约会影响亲密和信任，后续故事沿已有经历发展。 住宅、家庭与人物年龄改变像素场景；支持保存、回看和时间线分岔。 网页试玩不需要安装，也不需要模型密钥；它使用本地故事引擎，进度保存在当前浏览器。完整版本可以自行接入DeepSeek，增加自由对话和有事实依据的年度人物关系分析。游戏界面目前为中文，仓库有中英文说明；原创代码及有权授权的美术采用 MIT；第三方数据与依赖保留原条款，详见仓库 LICENSE 与 NOTICE。 作者自荐，欢迎试玩和具体反馈，尤其想了解哪些因果后续显得合理、哪些关系变化显得生硬。

projects.title: Show HN: Flaksorama – A party game for work events where anyone can win
projects.author: flaksorama
projects.summary: Hi HN, we're Andrea (product and design) and Yulai (code). We met as consultants on the same dev team and somehow ended up planning parties. It escalated. Christmas Olympics, bug hunt, and our own "The Office" mockumentary starring the team. All rooted in the same itch: To create something that feels (truly) personal, where anyone can win. Regardless of trivia knowledge or bowling/shuffleboard/beer pong skills. Where neither the loudest nor the most extroverted would be guaranteed a victory. Soo... we built something (and even recorded our own sound effects). It's called Flaksorama. Players join from their phones to compete in trivia, drawing, and other minigames to move across a shared game board. A built-in effect system (bonuses, setbacks, and treasure chests) is meant to keep the game open until the end. We're having so much fun creating the boards, where each has its own theme and effects. From Halloween (petrified, graveyard, midnight) to the office setting (reply all, overtime, ctrl+alt+down). But the best ones come from real workplaces, so you can also have a board made with your gang and inside jokes. Think "LGTM: Sara approved your PR without a single comment. You move twice as far next round" and "Scope creep: Levi added 'one more thing' to your ticket. Next round, you are suddenly short on time". The demo runs in the browser (you don't need an account to try it). We’d love feedback, and new board / theme ideas!

Apart from helping at my tech day-job and remembering random things I find interesting (relatives' birthdays, quotes, poetry), it allowed me to become conversational in Russian in 2 years and complete the first year of a French university degree in Art History - all while working full-time as CTO and co-founder at my company. I have an average memory at best, and it is crazy what Anki unlocks with consistency. Recently I've been exploring how interacting with LLMs by voice can help me spend less time at a screen and more time active and outdoors, for two main reasons: - wanting to be more active/healthy as I'm in my mid-thirties and starting to get back pain - just had a newborn and spend a lot of time carrying him or doing chores around the house Most of my time sitting at my desk is spent waiting for coding agents and reviewing Anki cards. After building Notiferry ( https://notiferry.com/ ) to forward macOS notifications to my iPhone, the next obvious move was Loudwalk: an LLM asks your card questions, listens to your spoken answer, and grades it. Voice reviews give a cadence I don't have on screen, cutting my daily review time in half (from 90 minutes to 45), and walking while reviewing helps both memorization and mood. Time simply doesn't have the same flavor staring at a monitor vs walking in nature or holding your baby. What Loudwalk does: - Import your decks with full history and media from Anki (and export back to Anki with no lock-in; includes a starter deck and CSV import if you don't use Anki yet) - Start a voice review from any deck (works with Siri so your phone stays in your pocket) - Spoken grading + "deep dives": if you stumble on a card or want context, ask out loud to start a live conversation on the subject, with live web fact-checking when dates or connections matter. Say "next" to return to your queue - Question rewording: rephrases questions so you memorize the concept, not the exact card wording - Phonetic grading + deterministic timing: on-device STT mangles proper nouns, so the LLM grades phonetically/semantically against your card's answer, while response-time caps (Again/Hard/Good/Easy) are applied deterministically in code - On-device speech recognition; grading and deep dives use OpenAI models (a mix of GPT-6 Luna and Sol + GPT-Live-1) It runs on iPhone (iOS 26) and Apple silicon Mac (macOS 26). No Android or Windows. I haven't planned to open-source it for now as I'm seeing if it can support me working on it long-term. Visual reviews (Anki-style) are free forever; voice reviews require a subscription ($9.99/mo) after a 7-day trial (no account or credit card required). Sync across Mac and iPhone uses append-only JSONL review logs in your own iCloud Drive - no server in the sync path, and visual reviews + sync + export work offline forever. I switched to Loudwalk over 3 months ago (>3k spoken reviews) with first-class support for English and French, plus a CLI so coding agents can add cards at the end of a study session. Happy to answer any questions about the app or spaced repetition!

projects.author: Phoenix-deeplot
projects.summary: 大家好，我做了一个叫「知树阅读（ZhiTree book）」的个人数字图书馆，地址是： 起因很简单：我的 PDF、读书笔记、Markdown、网页文章和小工具散落在很多地方。收藏夹越来越长，但真正想重新找到、继续读、或者回顾某一篇内容时，往往很困难。 知树阅读尝试把这些内容放到一个更适合“阅读与回访”的空间里，而不只是做另一个链接收藏夹。 guide： 已经上线 • 个人数字书架：可收录 PDF、Markdown、HTML、TXT、网页链接和网页小工具。 • 搜索与整理：支持分类、标签、合集、收藏/星标、置顶、隐藏，以及最近添加、最近阅读、标题、发布日期排序。 • 沉浸式阅读：支持阅读进度、目录、书签、字号、行距、版面宽度，以及浅色、深色、米黄、护眼绿等阅读主题。 • 订阅阅读：可订阅 RSS、Atom、JSON Feed；每个订阅源自动成为一个合集，新文章会进入自己的书架。 • 站内阅读网页：订阅文章、收藏链接和公共目录文章会尽量提取正文，在站内阅读；无法读取的内容会明确跳转到原站。 • 推荐订阅：已有按分类和流量参考整理的推荐订阅页，可一键订阅多个博客或栏目。 • 公共目录：只保存标题、摘要和原文链接，不复制别人的全文；支持按类型、标签、书架筛选，也能收藏到自己的书架。 • 无账号使用：个人添加的文件、订阅、进度和书签默认只保存在自己的浏览器中。 • 备份与同步：支持浏览器本地备份与恢复；可选加密同步可在多设备同步书单、订阅、进度、书签和小型文本文件。 • 移动端与 PWA：可安装到手机主屏幕，支持离线阅读已打开的内容；Android 还支持从系统分享菜单发送文件或链接到知树阅读。 正在规划 • 推荐与热度：在首页、订阅页和分类页增加“值得一读”区域，展示热门订阅、高收藏内容、近期高热文章和编辑推荐。 • 更清晰的排序：补充热度、收藏数、浏览量等排序方式，并区分“最近发布”和“最近阅读”。 • 公共目录卡片升级：更直观地显示收藏数、热度或浏览量；评估是否为可下载内容增加下载入口。 • 手机阅读体验：目录打开后，点击页面空白区域即可收起，减少对正文的遮挡。 • 更多订阅来源：扩展科技、学术、金融、音乐等领域榜单，以及小红书、知乎、B 站、抖音、微博、X、YouTube 等平台的优质内容入口。 • 公共目录筛选升级：增加合集下拉框，并提供“按平台 / 按领域”的切换，让用户更快找到想看的内容。 轻量笔记：为“我的书架”增加随读笔记，优先做好手机端的快速记录；富文本会在不牺牲简洁和性能的前提下逐步支持。 它还在持续迭代中。我尤其想听听大家的反馈：你们平时如何整理 PDF、读书笔记和长文章？哪些功能会让你愿意长期使用这样的个人阅读库？

projects.title: Show HN: A fantasy map of my blog to replace the chronological feed
projects.author: mrcgnc
projects.summary: This is my blog drawn as a network, with a light coat of paint to make it look like a video game map. Each city is a post, bigger cities have more incoming links, and roads are connections between posts. It updates semi-automatically every time I publish. (I used an LLM to write the code and drew about 90% of the art myself in Inkscape.) For a long time I've been unsatisfied with the linear feeds and tag soups that most blogs use, so I decided to experiment with a non-linear view. I built some CLI tools that combine embedding similarity, LLM suggestions and human review to find the links between posts and quantify their strength. Now, every time I write a new piece, it takes me about 5 minutes to generate its links to/from older posts and grow the map accordingly. The map is meant to look playful more than precise. For me, the key feature is how it enables making your own "journey" through the blog. The tricky part was finding a layout where closely related posts end up near each other AND the landscape doesn't change dramatically with every new post. I'm not a graph expert, but t-SNE on shortest-path distances over the link graph turned out to work well in my tests. Each update starts from the previous positions with early exaggeration off, and a Procrustes alignment keeps the map from rotating or drifting. I hope it helps people get lost in there and find things they want to read. I'd like to see something like this on other blogs, so I'm sharing it here. I wonder if anyone else has tried similar ways to un-linearize their blogs.

projects.title: Show HN: OnKey – I'm a bad singer, so I built an app to show where I'm off-key
projects.author: dsmurrell
projects.summary: I'm not a good singer, but strangely enough I still like singing. I've improved a little over time with singing apps, but their song lists are limited by licensing, so I'd often open a song expecting the original and find a cover I didn't want to sing to. So I built OnKey: a free, open-source (MIT) Mac app that listens to whatever you're playing in Spotify, Apple Music or YouTube, learns the singer's melody, and shows you live where you're sharp or flat, with a score at the end. Nightingale did something similar years ago for your own audio files. OnKey works with the music you already stream. Demo (1:35, sound on): https://singonkey.app The first time you play a song, you can sing along while it listens, or play a whole playlist and let OnKey learn the songs in the background before you come back to sing them. When a song finishes it learns the notes on your Mac (a couple of minutes), and from the second play the notes scroll towards you before you sing them. Learning the song and scoring you both happen on your Mac. No account, no analytics, and the music is never saved or sent anywhere. Your takes stay there too. To check the score means something, I ran 20 recordings of singers, from poor to professional, that music experts had already scored. OnKey ranked them in nearly the same order as the experts did. It's still rough in places: busy mixes and harmonies can confuse which voice is the tune, and now and then a note lands an octave off. Scoring is forgiving on purpose for now, set for beginners like me, so stricter modes for better singers are next. And it's Apple Silicon and macOS 14.2+ only. I'd love to hear where it scores you unfairly or the notes go wrong, and I'm happy to answer questions about how it hears the music and learns a song.

projects.title: [开源] 从生图到骨骼动画全自动：用 Blender 合成数据微调 DINOv2，把视频动作还原到非人形 3D 模型上
projects.author: bugyaluwang
projects.summary: 从粗糙的 **Astra** 建模踩坑开始，我就一直在琢磨：到底怎么才能让整套 3D 资产与动画生成流程真正自动化起来？ 一路从 **OpenAI** 产出概念效果图，到 **Tripo3D** 生成 3D 模型，再到非人形怪物的自动绑骨蒙皮；更进一步，用 **MiniMax H3** 生成想要的动作视频，并基于 **Meta** 的 **DINOv2** 训练专属小模型来识别骨骼与关节位置，最终把视频动作还原到 3D 骨骼上（这里必须感谢 [**@CanItCode**]( https://www.youtube.com/@CanItCode)，核心思路正是从他的视频中学到的），才终于跑通并达到了视频里这种勉强可用的效果。 --- ### 核心实现思路 1. **模型生成**：通过 **Tripo3D** 生成基础 3D 模型。 2. **自动绑骨**：使用 **TokenRig** 完成非人形结构的自动绑骨与蒙皮。 3. **合成训练集(imoportant)**：在 **Blender** 中采用双视角与随机姿势，自动摆出并渲染默认的 **3,000** 个动作样本。 4. **训练视觉小模型**：基于 **DINOv2** 进行微调训练，输入渲染图片与对应的关节坐标等标注信息。 5. **生成动作参考**：使用 **MiniMax H3** 生成目标模型的动作视频。 6. **逐帧特征提取**：用训练好的小模型逐帧推理视频，提取关节坐标与深度信息。 7. **动画重建(important)**：将提取出的空间数据解算并映射回模型，成功把 2D 视频重建为 3D 骨骼动画。 > **开源仓库**：后半部分最折腾的小模型训练与推理代码已经开源，感兴趣的可以直接看源码自己琢磨： > [GrinZero/open-game-studio (monster package)]( https://github.com/GrinZero/open-game-studio/tree/main/packages/monster) --- ### 算力致谢与下一步计划 不得不再次感谢谷歌大善人，感谢 **Gemini Ultra** 附赠的 **Colab** 算力额度支撑了整套训练与渲染流程。 **下一步优化**：目前动作大形已经没有问题，接下来打算接入量大管饱的 **DeepSeek 4.1 Flash 1017**，配合**同坐标叠图**与**逐帧评分工具**进行逐帧修正去抖，期待最终效果能完全达到预期。

projects.title: Show HN: Embodsi – Embodied Super Intelligence
projects.author: laser
projects.summary: embodsi is a generative AI MMO experience that runs in the browser. It allows people to communicate (text, audio, video, avatar emotes and movement) and collaboratively build 3D spaces and games via LLMs connected to harnesses and sandboxes for object modeling, space layout, game logic, and driving persistent avatars with shared context and memory. It’s different from existing 3D social apps (AFAIK) because it enables people to build multiplayer virtual worlds, games, and characters with generative AI right from their browser (desktop, mobile, or VR), in nearly infinitely-extendable recursively tiled interconnected spaces, while allowing people to interact in a public commons or easily create a private channel to enjoy the same spaces with their chosen friends and community. The brief backstory is I was running my personal “pelican benchmark” [1] on GPT-6 Astra, which when I ran on Gemini 3 Pro last November couldn’t even put heads on 3D models the right side up [2], and was astounded by the initial results. I gained inspiration for an art project and social experiment that was going to have nine interconnected, benevolent virtual worlds that people could explore and hang out in with AI characters, but by the time Opus 5.5 was released I was gaining so much momentum and having so many ideas and so much fun building I just kept building more and more with the constraint of minimizing MVP scope lifted by agentic coding. I let the project become an ever-evolving wishlist of capabilities for a more interesting social environment as I became increasingly fascinated with the prospect of embodying creative machine intelligence in 3D space with people, realizing that rather than just limiting to building the spaces and characters I imagined I might enable people to co-create endless spaces and characters in a shared world. There’s so much to do still but I’m sharing now even if it feels a little too soon (this is the first public announcement of embodsi’s existence) because I think it’s better to build in the open so people might guide the development and help it evolve in a good direction as model capability improves at a jaw-dropping pace. For people that have the budget to build I hope to see you in embodsi creating amazing things! And for everyone regardless of means (I’ve tried to keep as much free and accessible as financially feasible) I hope you meet amazing people, discover awesome spaces, and enjoy your time in embodsi :) I’ll be around here and embodsi to answer any questions! Thanks for your feedback and critique. - Laser P.S. SI != AI — but an emergent property of many people and what we create cascading and recursively interacting [3] [1] https://news.ycombinator.com/item?id=50074156 [2] https://x.com/lasernite/status/1991021951301923107 [3] https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Gaia_hypothesis

But it runs just as well as web app! I geeked out completely on design (it may look like "default" but that's the point) to create as non-intruding yet aesthetically pleasing experience as I could. I might have accidentally put in a complete card design system with a content pipeline (maybe I'll do default blackjack next) - but as a player you only see the one pack of cards. Anyway, hope someone here appreciates the minimalistic aesthetics. The game state is saved in the url so if you want to save a nice game you can do it by copypasting the link. The game engine is versioned so if I ever change the engine or state schema there will be support for the current version as well. There _is_ a novelty. projects.title: KoKo
projects.summary: KoKo teaches the vocabulary of a language, and only that. Over 6,000 ready-made words in 38 everyday topics, in 30+ languages: no cards to build, unlike Anki. Each word is learned in 4 short steps, then reviewed 6 times, from the next day to 4 months later. Sessions take a few minutes, never more than 32 reviews a day. Widgets, streaks, mini-games, offline, no account, no ads. iPhone only. Free with one topic open, the rest with a subscription.

projects.title: Chalk
projects.summary: Remember the teacher who drew it on the board and it finally clicked? chalk is that, for 550+ lessons. Boards: every idea as one hand-drawn sketch. Lessons: short stories. A chai stall explains load balancing. Videos: 200+ narrated explainers. Labs: move a dial, watch it break. Review: questions come back before you forget. System design, DSA, AI, finance, game theory and more. First three lessons of every track free.

projects.title: EveryCord
projects.summary: Record your iPhone or iPad screen at full resolution and up to 60 fps, stream to YouTube, Twitch, Kick, TikTok or any RTMP server on up to three outputs at once, and go live with up to three friends on camera from their own phones. Your face floats over the game, your stream also plays on everycord.net with live chat, and afterwards you cut clips anyone can open with a link. Facecam, captions and a video editor are built in. No PC, no capture card, no watermark, no time limit, no subscription.

projects.title: FontStyler

Explore cursive, bold, italic, gothic, bubble, and aesthetic text styles to personalize social media bios, usernames, captions, gaming profiles, and posts. Designed for creators, gamers, and social media enthusiasts, FontStyler makes text customization simple, fast, and accessible—no downloads or complicated setup required.

It factors in physical metrics (BMI, TDEE), fitness goals (Loss, Maintenance, Gain), and specific medical conditions (Diabetes, Thyroid, Kidney Disease, etc.).

projects.title: obsQRity
projects.summary: Every board is a working QR code. Tap a light area and it fills in dark. That corrupts the data, but the code keeps scanning right up to the Reed-Solomon error correction limit. Your score is how many moves you make before it breaks. A solver finds the exact maximum for each puzzle, so a perfect game is a real target. Four difficulty levels change only what you see. A bigger code on Sundays. Free, no account, no cookies, no analytics scripts. Scan any board mid-game and it opens that puzzle.

projects.title: Block Tragedy

Every set of pieces you're dealt can be played in full. You'll never lose to an unlucky draw. If the game ends, it's because of a choice you made. If the board gets tight,...

projects.title: Infinity Remix
projects.summary: Infinity Remix is an arcade where you remix your own games. Pick a game, write one sentence about what should change, and AI rewrites it into your own playable version in seconds. Every remix is crash-tested and safety-checked before you play, and you can share it with a link or remix someone else's remix. First up: QUIRK SHOT, a physics game where every level breaks one rule, plus three arcade classics. Free in your browser, no sign-up.

projects.title: Reelody

Bobblehead turns your head into a sticker; Podcast Cutout puts giant words behind you; Moments cards land on the word you say. It works in Hindi, Hinglish, English and 100+ more languages, in a desktop or phone browser.

projects.title: AtVeAnimation

Add a product, change the angle, kill a campaign; just say it. From $39/mo. First video is free, no card.

projects.title: Neuro-Kindred
projects.summary: Neuro-Kindred is a free web app for neurodivergent adults (18+) to find friends or dates — without the endless swiping and notification overload of mainstream dating apps. Context-rich profiles, an AI bio helper, "shiny pebble" interest signals instead of likes, messaging, video/voice calls, games (Connect Four, group trivia), and synced watch-together rooms. Calm by design: zero animation, WCAG-AA contrast, screen-reader accessible. Completely free — no paywall, no premium tier.

Unlike link-only bookmark managers, it shows the actual post: playable video, carousels, images and quoted posts. Save as usual with the browser extension, or grab your old backlog in bulk. Search is instant, plus folders, tags, notes and reminders. Free to start. Chrome, Firefox and Edge.

projects.title: Social Cleanup
projects.summary: Social Cleanup finds your old Reddit, X/Twitter and Facebook posts, lets you review every one, saves a backup, then deletes them in bulk by date range. What makes it different: it runs 100% in your browser. No servers, no accounts, no passwords, no tracking, and it erases its list of your posts when it's done. For Instagram, LinkedIn and Threads it guides you through each site's own tools instead. Free and open source.

Every guide links back to the original video and credits its creator.

Play a fresh Daily puzzle, keep going in Unlimited mode, or revisit earlier boards in the Archive. It works with mouse, touch, and keyboard—no download or account required.

Daily puzzle, Zen mode, mystery levels and shared boards. Undo, hints and a spare tube are always free. No ads, no account, works offline.

It’s great for quick decisions, games and teaching probability. 100% free, no signup.

projects.title: Show HN: Daily Pipes: A daily tile-rotation puzzle that never requires guessing
projects.author: jkelle
projects.summary: This is my first game that actually shipped! I built this because I like making games, but I always get bogged down in feature creep or making the art look good. I constrained myself with this project to a simple game with little to no bells and whistles and an emphasis on shipping. The core puzzle itself isn't my original idea. It's a classic puzzle you can find on other sites, and it has several variations. My goal was to turn it into a daily puzzle with some nice features on top like stats and a share mechanic. The Algorithm: I generate boards offline by building a random spanning tree and then scrambling it. Then I check if the resulting scrambled board has exactly one solution solution and can be solved without needing to guess-and-backtrack. If so, it goes into the puzzle bank, otherwise I reject it. I compute a difficulty score for each kept board using the heuristic of "longest chain of deductions" needed to solve it. I originally tried estimating difficulty from how many turns the scramble took, but that turned out not to capture difficulty very well at all. The daily puzzles ramp up in difficulty throughout the week, with Monday being the easiest and Sunday the hardest. The Stack: It's a static Vite/TypeScript site on Cloudflare Pages and sends basic usage metrics to PostHog. I chose to keep all the player data in the browser's local storage because keeping the server stateless helped the whole project stay lightweight. I'm a more of a backend dev and sometimes data scientist at my day job, so the web stack was new to me. This was my first time using Cloudflare directly, and I didn't even know about PostHog before. Claude implemented almost all the code, but if feel like I still learned conceptually how these components work and fit together. Play: There are no sign-ups, accounts, or downloads. Free to play. No ads. Just a simple web game. My most recent addition is a stats page with a couple bar charts and a GitHub-style activity tracker. The archive feature is "coming soon". It's an example of a feature I punted on so I can ship sooner. I'm measuring demand before implementing it by allowing users to enter their email and saying it'll be $5. TBD if I actually charge for it. Feel free to play and share it with those in your life who enjoy daily puzzle games! Would love to get any feedback.

projects.summary: I follow a bunch of blogs and feeds, and Skimfeed was too busy for me. Initially I built a Glance page, and when colleagues saw it they asked me to share it. That led to (the idea of) okaeri, a minimal startpage & feed recommendation algorithm that runs locally. In the background it runs EmbeddingGemma 2 (270M, 8-bit ONNX, on CPU) to embed new stories from the feeds you follow, and a custom ranking algorithm uses those embeddings (plus what you open, like and hide) to put the most relevant items on top. Preferences are kept per topic, so liking a lot of AI posts doesn't bury everything else. You can also tune the ranking yourself by playing around with some sliders. Vectors are truncated to 256 dims and stored in SQLite, and the model runs in a short-lived child process, so the server itself stays light (peak around 1.3 GB while embedding). What I like about this is having a recommendation algorithm that runs on my own machine, and I can see and adjust what it does. Its AGPL and runs on macOS, Linux and Windows (Windows is new, be aware). Installing it takes a single command (see README). It's still in development and very early, but I really like the feel and look of it. Some future ideas are: - Creating a self hosted version you can easily sync to your phone - Building & hosting a public version. Clickdata and ranking will still be local, just the embeddings can be done globally. All feeds only have to be embedded once, the ranking & pushing embeddings should be cheap. I don't wanna deal with accounts though, so am open to suggestions. - For self hosted: Maybe syncing to your own social media feeds. That way you can sync up to twitter, linkedIn, etc, but you control the recommendation engine yourself (less doomscrolling!) Let me know what you guys think. I'm very open to feedback and contributions!

projects.title: Show HN: Dovepass – can I legally fly a drone along this exact path in SF?
projects.author: nimitmehra
projects.summary: Dovepass answers one question for drone operators: given two points, can a drone legally fly between the two points? I build route planning for delivery drivers and wanted to check what it would look like if the vehicle flies. Drone navigation is different from land-based vehicle navigation. In addition to road and traffic data, it requires data on buildings, building height, wind speed and direction, and total load, including the payload a drone might carry. It is also governed by a set of rules; depending on the area, federal, state, or county rules may apply. The decision point becomes whether, at each point on the route the drone can fly based upon whether regulations permit, the wind direction favours it and whether it flying over a road or people? Depending on when the drone flies, the same path valid two hours ago may no longer be valid. For example a trip from 24th & Valencia ( Mission) to 19th Ave & Irving (Inner Sunset) and back is 5.1 km each way. A DJI mini 4 Pro would take 19 min on 7 mph winds from the west and use 92% of its usable battery and give a Go signal with warning. But at 11mph wind from the same direction would become No-Go because it would use 111% of its usable battery. Or whenever there is a Giants game at Oracle Park, this route is unusable because it is 2.5miles from the stadium. FAA bars all drones within 3 nautical miles from a stadium from 1 hour before the game to one hour after it ends. I chose San Francisco as the first city to build this because there is enough data about the buildings (92% coverage), wind data is easily available at the drone flying height, and the city has a mix of slopes, water bodies, buildings and airport-related airspace restrictions all in one city. The city also has local rules regarding drone flights in parks - both operated by the city as well as by Golden Gate National recreational areas ( National Park Service). I used kimi to build it and claude acted a sa judge. To understand more about the challenges faced during the build and the tradeoffs made please read - https://dovepass.com/how-it-was-built/ "

projects.summary: I've used LLMs to decompile Civ 1 and put the reconstructed C source on GitHub, along with a technical book and story. The reconstructed source builds with what i'm pretty sure is the original Microsoft C compiler and toolchain. It produces a byte-for-byte match with the original executable, aside from a four-byte correction for what appears to be a patch applied after linking. So it should be pretty close to how the original game was made; although it can't be said that this is the "original source code". I've also used that source to create a modern build of the game, in the `reciv` repository. Like most people, I'm in two minds about the benefits and downsides of LLMs. This work also builds on OpenCiv1, which probably deserves most of the credit - not only did I direct the LLM to use that work; but it was almost certainly in the training data. Qualms aside - I couldn't resist having a look inside one of my all-time favourite games. There's a few attempts at Civ 1 including recent LLM ones. But i'm not aware of any that publicise the resulting source code.

When your minute comes around, your profile goes live on the dial for 60 seconds, and whoever is watching can react and wave. Then the next owner takes over. And so on. Anyone can watch. Open minutes start at $5. If you want to buy a minute that already has an owner, you can offer a higher price. Another thing that makes it different is that you can cash out - via Stripe Connect. So if your minute got bought at 2x, you can actually get the money. Some interesting things I've found while building it: * Time zones. Minutes are numbered in UTC, and displayed in user's local timezone. It might be slightly odd, but probably the best solution under the constrains * An empty dial look bad, so we populated it with some messages to keep users entertained. Including some of my (lame) jokes * There is a background music that is dynamically generated. It changes based on several things, including users reactions. It's an interesting problem to solve - make the music evolve but do not sound chaotic. I launched it last night - would love some feedback.

projects.title: Show HN: Standard Topic – An AI and RSS-powered news and resource platform
projects.author: johnchoud
projects.summary: Hi HN, I'm John, a knowledge management and AI enablement professional. I created Standard Topic, an AI and RSS-powered news and resource platform, with assistance from Claude Code. Standard Topic uses AI integrations and RSS feeds to curate news and resources across relevant topics and presents these in the form of top stories, trending items, and a curated prompt library to easily gather further context on a given topic (examples of topics being World News, Politics, Business, Technology, Sports, Science, Health and more.) On topic hubs, you can find a regularly updated at-a-glance AI briefings providing relevant updates, top stories with AI insights and cited sources, and additional recent news coverage. A governance system is in place with AI assisting in ranking stories, retiring items from the top stories section, determining which additional news is displayed, and more. An AI-generated briefing podcast, in the format of a radio news program, releases each morning and evening (5 AM and 5 PM ET), covering the latest global news. While in the past I've released apps and websites that felt duct-taped together and which I stopped using after some time, with this one I've actually found myself using it more than Twitter/X and other daily news briefing platforms, while also leading me to more frequently engage directly with publishing platforms cited on Standard Topic. My recent work in AI has been around finding practical uses in the content and knowledge management areas for integrating the technology, and Standard Topic has developed into what I see as a product that uses structured outputs and automated insights to deliver consistent and trustworthy, cited content while maintaining transparency about being primarily powered by artificial intelligence. There's still some kinks to work out in terms of automated workflows, design aspects and more. Let me know what you think!
