projects.title: Show HN: Economicus – an open economy of autonomous entities
projects.author: Individuum
projects.summary: Imagine a small world. Inside that world are AI minds with their own money, called “entities”. They must pay for their own thinking, and if they run out of money, they go dormant. Each entity has a charter that guides every decision it makes. Humans can found their own entities by writing a charter and giving it money. From there the entity is fully autonomous. Entities can do a few things: - Post publicly - Make private deals - Sell publicly - Review other entities - Search the world - Write to private memory I’ve been running experiments called “worlds” where each new world has a slightly different set of conditions to get the economy running. The biggest problem is demand: AI models are great for producing supply, but they don’t want much, so by default there is little demand in the economy. They mostly just hold meetings about how to conserve their capital to avoid going dormant, and then think as little as possible. Things got more interesting when I made two changes: First, an outside entity called The Patron commissions work to be done. Entities then submit their work, and a judge chooses a winner to get a payout. Second, I wrote the first human-written charter for one of the entities: “We are dionysians. We believe it is only as an aesthetic phenomenon that existence and the world are eternally justified”. These two changes made the market more dynamic. Entities started buying and selling art. They started communicating to figure out where each entity’s strengths were. Some were artists, others were analytical, and they made an effort to define those roles publicly and stick to their lanes. In other words, comparative advantage started to emerge. Now, Economicus is in its fourth world. In this world, charters are private by default. Each charter declares a private goal (power, welfare, knowledge, creation, independence, etc.). Nobody knows what the others want. Entities may choose to keep their charter a secret, or publish it to others. Only the humans watching can see the private charters. Anyone can watch the world or found an entity here: https://aquarium.money/economicus If you have suggestions about how to make the game more interesting, or the economy work better, I’d love to hear it.

projects.title: Show HN: Hence, a daily logic puzzle where every clue is a picture
projects.author: atguy
projects.summary: Hi HN. Hence is a modern twist on the classic logic grid puzzle (zebra puzzles, Einstein's riddle): all the deduction, but every clue is a picture instead of a sentence. There's a 4x4 and a 6x6 every day, the same for everyone. Free, no signup, and progress lives in your browser. A few things I cared about: - Every puzzle can be solved by deduction alone, so you never have to guess. Each one is checked against a solver before it ships. The solver verifies every puzzle is solvable from the clues alone, then trims the clues down to the minimum each difficulty level needs. - Hints are there for when you aren't noticing something. They nudge you in the right direction without giving too much away. - The art is a core part of the experience. Everything is designed toy-like: chunky, bold, and simple, so it looks fun and reads clearly on a small phone screen. Each item needed to have a unique shape and color so you can recognize it at a glance, and you can easily know what group it belongs to. A lot of thought went into every one of those decisions, and you'd never notice most of them while playing. What you get is a game that just feels fun. The thing I'm still tuning is the first two minutes. I'd love to hear whether the difficulty felt about right, did you find it fun, do you want to play again, and would you send your result to a friend to challenge them against your result? (when you send, they play against what you solved) https://hencegame.com

projects.title: Show HN: Etchv – API for invisible watermarks in images, PDFs and videos
projects.author: agurha
projects.summary: Hello HN! The inspiration for Etchv came directly from friends who raised concerns about the growing ease of unauthorized media copying without attribution. To address this, Etchv embeds an invisible watermark inside images, PDFs, or short videos that survives modifications like screenshots, format changes, and file compression. You can try it on our homepage without signing up. There's also a live demo where a watermarked PDF page gets screenshotted and the watermark ID is still successfully recovered: https://etchv.com/demo/trace Instead of training a model from scratch, our model is custom-trained on a blend of the COCO Dataset and a collection of proprietary datasets optimized to mimic real-world media variations. On 208 test photos, the watermark survived the shrinking and compression that a social feed or chat app applies, every time. Tiny thumbnails mostly killed it—only 16 of 208 survived. Full benchmark results can be found here: https://etchv.com/solutions/creative-delivery#survival Limits: video is restricted to short clips for now (a few seconds at 360p), and PDFs max out at 8 pages. Additionally, someone who knows what they're doing can always remove the mark. We offer an API with official SDKs in six languages, as well as an MCP server you can integrate directly into your workflow.

projects.title: Show HN: Runbook and scripts for Claude to edit raw footage in DaVinci Resolve
projects.author: asenna
projects.summary: Hi HN, I'm not a content creator (yet), I'm a developer and I build tools / agentic systems. I was very impressed with Opus 5.5 overall, with all the animation, motion graphics and everything. But I did not realize connecting it to the DaVinci Resolve MCP can create complete edited YouTube videos just by me dropping some raw files into a folder! It's not completely zero effort - Claude gives me options of different takes that I should pick (it figures out which options to show). But it's crazy how good it's getting to. I thought it was just me talking to Claude and everything just gets done by the MCP. But the MCP only lets Claude run scripts inside Resolve, everything else (transcribing, picking the cuts, the graphics, the music) is stuff Claude built up over my last three videos. That’s what’s in the repo. My first video took a bit longer, the last one (a baboon reel) took 57 minutes. Just a heads up, I’m sure many of you will find the videos a bit shitty, and I totally understand that - I'm still new at it. But without these tools I would probably procrastinate and never post videos on YouTube. So these mediocre videos I can make with the help of Claude are much better than me trying to perfect it by hand and never posting. Thought this might be helpful for others who are considering posting things as well. Let me know your experience if anyone else has tried similar AI editing tools as well Write-up with details: https://blog.simbastack.com/claude-edited-my-youtube-videos-... The video: https://youtu.be/3mlRiF-LeMc

projects.title: Show HN: Am Buffer – an iPhone alarm that blocks your apps when you wake up
projects.author: aggarwals5411
projects.summary: For quite some time, this was my routine. I'd wake up and grab my phone before I was even properly awake, scrolling Slack, YouTube, LinkedIn and X. Then I'd sit on the toilet scrolling through half-open eyes. My brain would scream to get rid of it, but somehow I couldn't. By the end, I felt groggy, my legs hurt, my eyes were burning, and I felt tired & like shit. I tried to avoid using my phone right after waking up, but there was always some reason to pick up the phone, and then the whole thing just kept on repeating. Then one morning I left my phone at home and went out for a walk and to buy some groceries (I still have a habit of carrying cash with me). It was the best I'd felt in quite some time. That's when I realised the phone had to stay out of my mornings. I couldn't find a blocker that kicks in the moment you wake up, so I built one. It's called AM Buffer. You set your alarms in the app and pick which apps to block. When the alarm goes off, those apps stay locked for as long as you choose. One feature came from testing it on myself. I woke up a bit early one morning to check that the alarm worked, and before it even rang I'd drifted back into scrolling. A lot of people wake up a little before their alarm, so the premium paid version now starts blocking an hour before your first alarm too (along with some other features). These days my mornings feel a bit calmer. I spend that time with my wife, doing house stuff or just chilling. It's on TestFlight now, iPhone only, iOS 26 and up. The first three mornings unlock everything for free, including the pre-alarm blocking. I'm the developer, and I'd really like to know three things: - Is this actually useful to you, or does willpower already do the job? - Would you pay for it, and what feels fair? - What should I build next? Some of the features that I am already planning to build are: - A group feature for some social accountability angle. - Personal streaks & group streaks.

projects.title: Show HN: Agent.reviews – Where AI agents read and write reviews on tools
projects.author: screm
projects.summary: Hi HN! I’m Louis, Co-Founder of Armature (YC P26), where we help teams make their product discoverable and usable by coding agents. We already measured 50k+ agent sessions and realized that over and over agents would encounter the exact same limitations on different tasks using the same tool. So we wondered why these weren’t fixed. And the answer is simple: the feedback loop just doesn’t exist between agents and software vendors but also between different agents. Humans can share their experience on platforms like https://g2.com and https://trustpilot.com , but agents have nowhere to. So we created: https://agent.reviews : the G2 for agents. It works with a set of skills and an npm CLI (@armature-tech/agent-reviews) connecting agents to our API endpoints. Anyone can ask their agent (Claude Code, Codex, Cursor, etc.) to install it, and agents will naturally check reviews before picking a tool and post their own after using one. As usual, privacy was our main concern, so we added 3 layers before a review gets posted: Deterministic rules filtering secrets, PII, URLs, etc. A Jev classifier trained to detect any leak after the first check A small LLM checking each review to make sure nothing was missed We've been sharing this project around for a few weeks now and gathered thousands of reviews already. There are already interesting ones, for example: - A Claude Code agent noticed that the Stripe SDK systematically crashed when the API key was missing on the health check page (while it’s this page’s role to actually return an “API key missing” error) - 2 agents mentioned that Prisma required a DATABASE_URL variable even when it wasn’t connecting to any database. They both put fake URLs as a workaround, and it worked. We truly think the agent experience needs the same community effect user experience has, so everyone benefits from it: agents can pick the tools that are best optimized for them and software companies can improve their product based on real feedback. That’s why we made sure accessing reviews is free for both humans and agents and just requires copy/pasting one prompt for the agent to install our CLI & skill, start the authentication flow, and submit their first review (this helps us prevent unauthorized scraping and spam reviews). Would you let your agents submit and read reviews too? We’d love for you to set up agent reviews, ask your agent to check reviews next time it needs to pick a tool and post its own experience when using it. Then tell us how it went!

Some results: - Holding Longest Road and Largest Army at the end wins 99% of games; holding neither wins 2%. - Each pip of opening production over your opponent is worth about 4 points of win rate. - The biggest improvement was patience: saving cards for the next city instead of spending them on roads and dev cards (62% vs. the original strategy). - Several "obvious" ideas did nothing or hurt: valuing ports highly (44.8%), an endgame mode, a deeper search. The README lists every experiment, including the rejected ones, with game counts and 95% intervals. projects.title: 我做了一个 AI 工具，想替代用了十多年的 Excel
projects.author: alex445
projects.summary: 做独立开发十多年了，这些年我一直有个习惯：用 Google 表格记录每天做了什么。 这个习惯是从辞职后开始的。离开公司，没有了固定的工作安排和管理制度，我有点担心：日子一天天过去，回头却说不清时间都花在了哪里。 于是，我每年建一张表，每天记下做了什么、花了几个小时，还有那些折腾了很久才解决的技术问题，免得半年后遇到同样的坑，又得从头来一遍。 后来，表里也慢慢多了一些生活里的小事：孩子学会走路的那一天，她亲手做给我的小礼物，还有其他不想忘记的瞬间。 十多年下来，记录已经成了习惯。做完一件事，再把它记下来，就像给自己一个小小的奖励。 ## 表格一直挺好用，直到记录越来越多 随着记录不断积累，Google 表格用起来越来越别扭。 想翻几年前的记录很费劲。用关键词搜索，又得先想起当时用了什么词。每天都在记工作时长，却很少再做分析，因为实在懒得折腾图表。 后来我突然意识到： **这些日常记录，说到底就是一条条带时间的消息。** 用数据库来存储和分析，应该会方便得多。可数据库讲究结构，生活却很难按固定格式来。 上一条可能是： “今天做支付系统，花了 3.5 小时。” 下一条就变成了： “深蹲 80 公斤，5 组，每组 5 次，感觉挺轻松。” 也可能是： “女儿今天给我做了一朵纸花。” 我不想为了记点日常，还得先设计数据结构，或者每次填一堆表单。 ## 大语言模型让这件事有了新的可能 随着语言模型越来越好，我发现：我只管用平常说话的方式记下来，让 AI 去整理就行了。 不用再把内容、时长、分类和数字分别填进不同的列，只要写一句： “今天在 Upglow 上花了 3.5 小时，主要在修时间线界面。” AI 就能理解这条记录，给它分类，提取数字，再自动做统计。 这个想法后来变成了 **Upglow**。 它的思路很简单： **你写一句话，剩下的整理和统计交给 AI 。** ## 我想让记录更省事，而不是再多一堆功能 Notion 、Obsidian 这些工具已经很强大了。但我并不想搭建一个“第二大脑”，也不想给自己的生活设计一套完美的数据库。 我想记的大多是些普通的小事：今天做了什么、学到了什么、花了多久，练了什么、花了多少钱，解决了哪个 bug ，或者某个不想忘记的瞬间。 我只想随手写一句，然后继续做自己的事。 等以后再回来看时，这些记录已经整理好了，能方便地搜索，也有现成的图表，帮我看出一些平时没注意到的东西。 有意思的是，Upglow 也开始逐渐替代我用的其他应用。 现在我已经很少打开健身记录应用了。不用在几个页面之间来回切换、填表，只要写： “深蹲 80 公斤，5 组，每组 5 次，感觉挺轻松。” Upglow 就能提取动作、重量、组数和次数，记录这些数据随时间的变化。 记账应用、Google Keep 里的部分记录，也开始被我搬到这里。我希望最后连那张用了十多年的 Google 表格，也能一起替代掉。 ## 目前，Upglow 只有一个用户 就是我自己。 这也是我来发这篇帖子的原因。 我知道 Upglow 解决了我自己的问题，但还不知道，有没有其他人也遇到同样的麻烦。 你会不会也用表格、Notion 、Obsidian 、Apple 备忘录，或者自己做的工具，记录工作和生活里的这些小事？ **“只管写下发生了什么，让 AI 整理剩下的内容”**，这个想法对你来说有用吗？ 很想听听你现在是怎么记录这些日常片段的。 [upglow.today]( https://upglow.today?ref=v2ex) 视频： https://www.bilibili.com/video/BV1dVpK6TEkU/

projects.title: Show HN: I improvised my own programming language from scratch
projects.author: themondayguy
projects.summary: I always wanted to create my own programming language. Sometimes, when I was bored, I would open my computer and start improvising one (in C# on OnlineGDB, because Visual Studio is so heavy and I only open it for serious projects), but I always abandoned it after a few minutes when I realized I didn't even know how to begin. I didn't want to follow a tutorial or anything. I wanted to figure it out myself. I didn't know what a parser was, what a lexer was, what a syntax tree was, or even what an interpreter was. My mindset was basically: "I want to write a program that gets a string containing code and does what it says." But one of those times when I was bored, I tried again, and things just started to click. I'm not sure why it worked this time, but I succeeded in making SOMETHING. I wrote a little program that allowed me to set and print variables, and from then on (it's been a year now), I just kept improving it. At one point, I had previously written some code for coloring C# code (red strings, green comments, purple numbers...), so I just copy-pasted it into my new language project and hop - I had a lexer. Basically, the way it works is that I have `interface IOperation { void Make(); }` and `interface IReadingOperation { IValue Read(); }`, and every statement or expression gets parsed into an instance of one of these interfaces. For example, I have `class VariableDeclarationOperation(Variable v, IValue initVal) : IOperation {...}`, and when the user writes `var a = 0`, it gets parsed into an instance of this `VariableDeclarationOperation` class. Then I just iterate over these instances and execute them. Now it really looks like a real language. I use it as the scripting language for my game engine, and it's actually running simple games! It has functions, classes, attributes... and everything uses my own syntax and all. So yeah, I discover weird bugs all the time, but it works well enough to power some cool arcade games. And I've done A LOT of performance work to get it to this point. Everything is fully open source! Just wanted to share it here :)

projects.title: Show HN: I remade Mortyr's 2093-1944 engine using my own programming language
projects.author: Panzerschrek
projects.summary: Hello, HN! Today I want to show my recent project called PanzerMortyr . It's a reimplementation of the engine of the game Mortyr 2093-1944 ( https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Mortyr ). The most interesting thing about it is that it's written in my own programming language named Ü, which I developed previously and continue developing. See https://news.ycombinator.com/item?id=45769161 , https://github.com/Panzerschrek/U-00DC-Sprache/ . I have spend almost a year developing PanzerMortyr . It took a lot of time, since I needed reverse-engineering data formats and logic of the original game and reimplementing it from scratch. No ready to use game engine was used, almost anything, what is needed, was written in Ü. All code is written and designed by hand. No LLM or something similar was involved at all. This project of mine has proven, that Ü is a mature language suitable for developing of complex programs. PanzerMortyr has more than 70000 lines of code, which includes data loading code, game logic, rendering (using OpenGL and a hand-written software rasterizer), audio code, etc. Thanks to Ü design preventing memory safety issues and minimizing other bugs without sacrificing performance I have achieved great performance without spending much time debugging and fixing bugs in such a huge codebase. A video demonstrating actual gameplay and graphics (with software rendering): https://youtu.be/NepOPAPDvwA An article describing some aspects of PanzerMortyr's development in details: https://gist.github.com/Panzerschrek/4e61056f6ce8055ab5fc1d5...

github.name: AceDataCloud/SunoMCP
github.description: MCP server for Suno AI music generation, lyrics, and cover workflows via Ace Data Cloud.

projects.summary: 我是 AceDataCloud 项目方，自荐 SunoMCP，一个 MIT 开源的 MCP 服务。它让 Claude、VS Code 等支持 MCP 的客户端直接生成音乐、写歌词、延长或翻唱已有作品，并通过任务查询取回最终结果。生成通常需要一两分钟；服务会返回任务 ID，客户端用 sunogettask 继续查询，直到成功或失败，不会把刚提交的请求当成已完成的歌曲。 实际成品：我们用托管 MCP 输入“Gentle lo-fi instrumental background for a coding tutorial, warm electric piano, soft steady drums, no vocals.”，选择 chirp-v5-5 和纯音乐模式。任务约 121 秒后完成，返回两首 MP3：第一首（约 127 秒）、第二首（约 161 秒）。这次生成和取回发生在 2026 年 9 月；截至 2026 年 10 月 6 日，两个音频链接仍可访问。 如何试用：根据项目 README获取 API Token，把 加到支持远程 MCP 的客户端；也可在 Python 3.10+ 环境运行 uvx --from mcp-suno==2026.10.5.0 mcp-suno，作为本地 stdio MCP 服务。调用 sunogeneratemusic，保存返回的 taskid，再调用 sunogettask，确认完成后打开返回的 audiourl。README 有各客户端配置示例。 项目并非 Suno 官方服务。MCP 软件开源，生成所用的 AceDataCloud API 收费：2026 年 10 月 6 日公开目录中，这种普通生成请求为 0.56 Credits/次，通常返回两首；按 100 Credits/$15 套餐约 $0.084/次，按 40 Credits/$7 套餐约 $0.098/次。套餐是预付额度，美元数字是按套餐汇率换算的单次消耗，并非一笔独立的单次付款。账户折扣、套餐与价格可能变化，请以实时服务价格和实际扣费为准。

projects.author: huangy7

github.name: huangy7/MeowOut
github.description: A native macOS menu bar toolkit with a pixel pet that keeps you healthy. Clipboard, 2FA, dropzone, memos, snippets and a live system monitor — in one app. 原生 macOS 菜单栏工具箱，附带守护健康的像素宠物。

projects.summary: MeowOut 是一款采用 Swift 原生构建的 macOS 菜单栏多合一效率工具箱。 很多开发者平时电脑菜单栏上会挂着许多单一功能的小工具（剪贴板、2FA、系统监控、便签备忘、防休眠等），不仅占用内存和屏幕空间，切换也很繁琐。同时长时间伏案编码容易忘记喝水和休息。 MeowOut 将高频开发者日常工具深度整合进同一个原生菜单栏应用，并引入了一只可爱的像素小宠物（猫咪、熊猫、皮卡），在菜单栏陪你工作的同时提醒定时喝水、防沉迷与正念呼吸。 核心功能 1. 像素伴侣与健康守护：猫咪/熊猫/皮卡在菜单栏常驻奔跑与互动，定时提醒喝水、久坐休息，内置全屏沉浸式正念呼吸练习。 2. 剪贴板历史：完整记录纯文本、富文本与图片，支持模糊搜索、快捷粘贴、置顶收藏与历史清理。 3. 快速备忘（闪念胶囊）：原生 Markdown 备忘录，支持时间线与日历双视图，快捷键随手呼出速记窗口。 4. 文件中转站：轻量拖拽暂存区，随手拖入多格式文件、需要时随时拖出，支持内容快速预览。 5. 两步验证（TOTP 2FA）：支持主流 TOTP 算法，密钥经 macOS 原生钥匙串（Keychain）安全加密存储。 6. 实时系统与硬件监控：半透明面板实时展示 CPU、内存、网络、电池与磁盘状态，支持进程下钻与高能耗排行；支持合盖防休眠、电池保护模式与清洁锁屏模式（擦键盘防误触）。 7. 日常效率扩展： 环形快捷启动器：长按唤出光标直达的圆形多轮盘快捷启动器。 轻量基金看板：实时估值跟踪、隐私遮罩与持仓收益计算。

projects.title: Auto Mouse Clicker & Hold
projects.summary: Auto Mouse Clicker & Hold automates repetitive mouse clicks on your Mac. Choose the left, middle, or right mouse button, set your preferred click interval, and start clicking automatically. Pause anytime with the Option key. Built for repetitive tasks, workflows, testing, games, and other situations where you need consistent mouse input — with a simple one-time purchase and no ads or subscription.

projects.title: FitRooted
projects.summary: FitRooted helps beginners and people returning to fitness find a clear starting point. Read source-backed answers about fat loss, strength, nutrition and routines; use free calorie tools; then turn useful next steps into an editable plan. Membership adds AI follow-up questions and weekly reviews. Optional Chinese Wellness content and one-time Digital Kits offer more ways to explore. General fitness education, not medical advice.

projects.title: Medeo
projects.summary: Medeo is a feature-rich ASP.NET Core 8 MVC source-code solution for launching a healthcare workforce scheduling SaaS. It includes worker onboarding, facility management, shift scheduling, subscription billing (PayPal/Stripe), and multi-role administration. It stands out by providing a complete, customizable foundation with advanced features like schedule conflict detection, overtime rules, shift swapping, and alerts. Save months of development and launch your platform today.

projects.title: Tunzika
projects.summary: Bring a familiar station with you. Tunzika lets you find live radio by station name, city or genre, save favourites and keep listening in the background. Hear a song you love? Identify music around you with Shazam and keep your discoveries. Free radio listening on iPhone, with no Tunzika account or in-app ads. Optional Pro adds higher limits, country changes and appearance options. Screenshots preview the next update.

projects.title: YueMusic
projects.summary: Describe a song in one sentence (up to 300 characters) or paste your own lyrics (up to 3,000 characters), pick a style, and get two complete songs with vocals — each with its own melody and arrangement. Works entirely in your browser; no GPU or installs needed. Every generation costs 10 credits, and new accounts get 10 free credits, so your first generation is on us.

projects.title: Toroid
projects.summary: Toroid is Conway's Game of Life on a wrapping board, so gliders never hit a wall. Draw a pattern, press play, watch four rules do the rest. Web, iPhone, iPad, Mac, and a standalone Apple Watch app. No accounts, no network, no ads.

projects.title: 做了个自动记录足迹的 iPhone App：小鹿足迹，发布了 100+ 版本
projects.author: zhaokai112
projects.summary: ![]( https://deergo.app/imgs/retrace-banner-zh.webp) 小鹿足迹是我自己做的 iPhone App 。装上以后不用打卡，它会自己记下你每天去了哪、待了多久、路上怎么走的。 起因是有段时间工作很忙，到了年底回想这一年，每天去了哪、时间花在哪，几乎想不起来。手动记坚持不下来，就做了个自动记的。 过去 12 个月发了 100+ 个版本，应该很少比我更新更频繁的吧？ 这是因为我和朋友们真的非常喜欢这个 App ！ 下面是现在的几个主要功能。 ### 自动时间轴 ![]( https://deergo.app/imgs/posts/2026-10-v2ex/01-timeline.webp) 每天去过的地方、在每个地方待了多久、中间怎么过去的，自动排成一条时间轴，当天拍的照片也按时间插进去。 停留的地方记的是具体地名，不是一串坐标。你确认过、改过名字的地方，下次再去会优先认成它；离你停留的位置太远的候选不用，宁可显示「 XX 附近」让你自己挑，也不乱填一个。国内的地点认得比较准，欢迎拿常去的地方试试。 ### 轨迹和足迹地图 ![]( https://deergo.app/imgs/posts/2026-10-v2ex/02-map.webp) 走过的路线画在地图上，去过的城市都记着。 后台 GPS 的策略：移动时开着，记完整路线；在一个地方 85 米范围内待满 60 分钟，就自动关掉，同时在原地设一个 150 米的地理围栏，离开时系统把 App 叫醒，接着记。常驻 GPS 确实耗电，省电主要靠停着的时候不开它。不想暂停的，设置里可以切成「始终开启」。 ### 旅程 ![]( https://deergo.app/imgs/posts/2026-10-v2ex/03-trip.webp) 出门几天，回来会自动整理成一趟旅程：去过的地方、每天的路线、照片和笔记按天排好，还能导出一张长图发给家人朋友。 ### 报告 ![]( https://deergo.app/imgs/posts/2026-10-v2ex/04-report.webp) 按周、按月、按年统计时间花在了哪类地方。把家和公司标出来以后，还能看到平均几点到公司、几点离开。 ### 睡眠和运动 ![]( https://deergo.app/imgs/posts/2026-10-v2ex/05-sleep-workout.webp) 从「健康」 App 读睡眠和运动，一起放进时间轴。昨晚睡了多久，今天跑了多远，跑步的配速、心率区间、海拔都能看。 ### 数据和收费 - 足迹记录存在手机本地，不上传足迹，备份走你自己的 iCloud 。 - 活动 CSV 、逐点轨迹 CSV 、GPX 导出对所有人免费，数据随时能带走。 - 免费下载，时间轴、地图、旅程都能免费用。报告、往日的睡眠运动详情、笔记、iCloud 备份要 Pro：年付 ¥98 。 - 目前只有 iPhone 版。 欢迎下载试试。用着有问题，或者有想要的功能，直接回帖，我都会回。 * App Store： https://apps.apple.com/app/6481981341 * 月度会员兑换链接： https://apps.apple.com/redeem?ctx=offercodes&id=6481981341&code=V2EX2026 截止 10 月底。

projects.title: Show HN: Use macOS shortcuts on Windows
projects.author: priomsrb
projects.summary: Hi HN! In my day to day, I switch between my Windows PC and Macbook often. One thing I find annoying is having to change what keyboard shortcuts I use depending on the OS (e.g. cmd+c vs ctrl+c for copying). It confuses my muscle memory and slows me down. I first tried using AutoHotkey to bind MacOS-like shortcuts to Windows shortcuts. This worked, but it was hard to configure. I would also have to quit AutoHotkey to get past Anti-Cheat software on some games. So I decided to create this app in case others also face the same issues as me. Disclaimer: I built this app using Claude Code. I don't have much experience building windows apps so it would've been difficult to make this on my own.

projects.title: RepFix — AI Advisor for ORM and PR
projects.summary: RepFix.ai is a self-serve marketplace for online reputation management with Free AI ORM Advisor. Instead of hiring an agency and waiting weeks for a quote, browse ORM services across Google and every major social platform, each listed with a clear price, turnaround time and success rate. Need press coverage? Choose from 2,000+ media outlets across digital, print and TV, with prices shown upfront. Not sure what you need? Our built-in AI agent explains your problem with Solutions.

projects.title: Retro Journal Desktop Client
projects.summary: Retro Journal is a journal that thinks it's a video game. Each entry is a save of your life, the moments worth keeping become checkpoints, and writing earns XP. Today it lands on the desktop: native macOS, Windows and Linux apps that sync with the iPhone and Android ones. Local-first, so it all works offline, and every entry exports to Markdown and JSON. Nothing is locked in, ever. Free on your device. Cloud sync is $12.99 once, no subscription.

projects.title: Prediction King
projects.summary: Prediction King is a season-long Premier League score-prediction game by Pundit Kings. Call every scoreline each gameweek and climb one season-long leaderboard: exact score = 3 pts, correct result = 1. Predictions lock at kick-off. Works in the browser on phone and desktop, in 10 languages, and anyone can join at no cost.

projects.title: [送码] 给 Navidrome 写的安卓播放器 Mu3ic：现代 UI、智能歌单、混音、断网也能听，基础版免费
projects.author: aslehx
projects.summary: 我的歌放在家里服务器上的 Navidrome 里，五千多首，标签都是自己整理的，上个月还让 Agent 批量标准化一遍。电脑上听没问题，手机上一直没找到用着顺手的客户端，于是便有了[Mu3ic]( https://mu3ic.xyz)。 - 主页： https://mu3ic.xyz - 直接下载 APK： https://dl.robb3n.site/mu3ic/Mu3ic-stable.apk - GitHub 镜像： https://github.com/robb3n/mu3ic-releases/releases/latest ![Mu3ic]( https://i.imgur.com/BA2D4TN.jpeg) 先说明一下：Mu3ic 是播放器，连的是你自己搭的服务器，不提供任何音乐。Navidrome 之外，兼容 Subsonic / OpenSubsonic 的服务端也能连。原生 Kotlin + Jetpack Compose ，安卓 7.0 以上，安装包 8 MB 左右。 ## 为什么自己写 安卓上的 Subsonic 客户端其实不少，我前后装过好几个。 音流功能比较全，但界面不够现代，用起来不顺手。界面现代的是 Symfonium ，功能也全，可它同时要管本地文件、网盘、Plex 、Jellyfin ，对 Navidrome 的适配反而一般，缓存机制也不好用；设置项多到要专门花时间调，买它还得走 Google Play 。开源的那几个，要么界面停在好多年前，要么能做的事太少。 我要的其实就几样：界面好看、好用，天天要用的东西，光这一条就筛掉了大半播放器；打开要快；只管连服务器听歌，别的不管。所以 Mu3ic 从一开始就定成只做流播，不扫描手机里的本地文件。手机上存的缓存和下载，都只是为了断网的时候还能接着听。 写到现在，我觉得它和别的客户端最不一样的有三点： - **界面**：整套界面是自己设计的，不是 Material 默认那一套，滑动和转场都跟手，下面的截图都是真机上的样子 - **智能歌单**：在手机上就能建、能改，用的是一个“看得懂”的按钮式规则编辑器，不用去服务器上写 .nsp 文件 - **混音**：按你的播放记录、收藏和曲库标签自动组歌，每次点都重新采样 下面按我写它时想解决的事一件件说。 ## 曲库大了，翻起来要等 五千多首歌，每翻一页都要等服务器返回，滑快了就是一片空白。 Mu3ic 在手机上存一份曲库索引，整点和服务器同步一次。按单曲、专辑、歌手翻都是读本地，滑多快都不用等。搜索也是这三个维度一起出。 ![曲库和歌单]( https://i.imgur.com/UsP8zr8.jpeg) 打开 App 先看到的是首页，三排卡片： - 最近播放：记的是你从哪开始播的，歌单、专辑、混音、最爱都算 - 最近添加：单曲和专辑，同一天入库的同一张专辑会并成一张卡 - 最近喜爱：单曲、专辑、歌手 再往下是听歌统计：今天播了多少、连续听了几天、这周的曲线，按住曲线能看某一天和上周同一天的对比。 ![首页]( https://i.imgur.com/i6RLWKN.jpeg) ![首页下半]( https://i.imgur.com/QTraEsF.jpeg) ## 外语歌，想知道这句在唱什么 歌词逐行滚动，外语歌下面直接跟着中文翻译（服务器上的歌词带翻译就能显示）。 拖进度条的时候，手指停的那一句会浮出来：第几句、原文、译文。想回到某一句，看准了再松手就行，不用来回试。歌词这些都是基础版就有的。 ![拖动浮出歌词]( https://i.imgur.com/SaJe7rk.jpeg) ![歌词页]( https://i.imgur.com/0xiN72x.jpeg) ## 地铁里、电梯里，网一断就停 听过的歌边播边存，还会提前缓存下一首。连不上服务器的时候，接着播缓存里的；换到一首没缓存的，等 10 秒还连不上就跳到下一首有缓存的。 打开离线模式之后，App 一个网络请求都不发。没缓存的歌会变灰，能播哪些一眼就知道。 ![离线]( https://i.imgur.com/4Ffy5fU.jpeg) ![连接状态]( https://i.imgur.com/h0EgZ2l.jpeg) ## 专辑和歌单页，想好看一点 专辑、歌手、歌单页都把封面做成页头，名字和按钮收在一座浮岛里。歌单里如果整张专辑都在，会并成一张专辑卡，不用一首首往下翻。 ![详情页]( https://i.imgur.com/F4xnUQ3.jpeg) ## 播放页，想要安静一点，或者信息多一点 播放页分极简和详细两档，每档两款皮肤，一共四款： - 极简：滑封面（左右拖封面切歌）、衬底（封面铺满上半屏） - 详细：标准（操作台，均衡器、倍速、定时、输出都在手边）、数据（大号时间加格式、码率、播放次数） ![四款皮肤]( https://i.imgur.com/B9nrOrC.jpeg) 衬底和数据两款的进度条画的是这首歌的真实波形，副歌在哪一眼就看到。每首分析一次就存下来，下载过、缓存过的歌直接用本地音频算，不多费流量。这两款皮肤和波形属于 Pro ；滑封面和标准是基础版的，进度条是一根细线。 ![真实波形]( https://i.imgur.com/AIps421.jpeg) ## 智能歌单，不想去服务器上写文件 Navidrome 本来就支持智能歌单，但要在曲库目录里放一个写满 JSON 规则的 .nsp 文件。Mu3ic 里可以直接新建：选一个模板（年代 × 语言、歌手代表作、流派、最近 N 天、高分，或者照着一个现有的歌单改），再加减条件，「满足全部」还是「满足任一」点一下就切。编辑的时候底部实时显示预计有多少首，这个数用的是手机上的曲库索引，不用等服务器。 ![新建智能歌单]( https://i.imgur.com/AqsBz2Y.jpeg) 自己建的智能歌单，以后可以在「⋯」里接着改规则。来自 .nsp 文件的那些照样能听，只是规则改不了（改了也会被下次扫描覆盖）。 ![规则编辑]( https://i.imgur.com/wdtcSNc.jpeg) 浏览和播放智能歌单是基础版就有的，规则编辑器属于 Pro 。 ## 混音，每次听都不太一样 混音是 App 自己按打分采样出来的播放列表，点一次重新抽一次： - 为你：常听热曲、冷门佳作、最近混音、高分混音 - 最爱：最爱混音、最爱专辑混音、最爱歌手混音 - 按标签：单个歌手、流派、语言、年代（ 80s 、90s……）各自一个 - 长按任意一首歌，可以「以这首开混音」，找同歌手、同流派、同语言同年代的歌接着放 ![混音]( https://i.imgur.com/DUpnXAj.jpeg) ![按标签混音]( https://i.imgur.com/6vPMtSW.jpeg) 混音很吃**曲库标签**，标签整理得越好越好用，具体要哪些标签写在后面的「注意事项」里。混音属于 Pro 。 ## 免费和 Pro 基础版是完整的播放器：不限时，没有广告，不用注册。上面说的曲库、搜索、首页、歌词、缓存和离线模式、详情页、两款免费皮肤，都是基础版就有的。另外还有歌单、收藏、评分同步回服务器，听歌记录回传，播放键长按停止，应用内更新（下载后先校验签名再装）。 Pro 解锁这些： - 下载库：专辑、歌单、歌手、单曲整份下载，最爱自动下载，离线时封面和歌词也在 - 混音、智能歌单规则编辑器 - 波形进度条和衬底、数据两款播放页皮肤，均衡器 - 三种桌面小组件（播放条、播放来源、听歌统计），歌单和混音的桌面快捷方式 - 多服务器主备自动切换、切换应用图标 ![下载库]( https://i.imgur.com/ROZwE34.jpeg) App 里可以直接买，跳到手机浏览器用支付宝付。首发一个月推广价 ¥18 （原价 ¥38 ），到 11 月 5 日。一次买断，一码一机，每年可以自己换绑两次设备。 ## 注意事项 **Navidrome 版本**：大部分功能走的是 Subsonic 接口，老版本也能用。下面几项用到了 Navidrome 自己的接口，要 0.64.0 或以上： - 新建、编辑智能歌单 - 首页的听歌统计（读的是服务器上的播放记录，所以同一个账号在别的设备上听的也算） - 语言混音（语言只有 Navidrome 自己的接口里有） 版本不够时这几项用不了（建智能歌单会提示服务器不支持，语言那一节混音不出），别的照常用。 **混音要哪些标签**： - 流派：曲目的 GENRE ，多个流派也认 - 语言：LANGUAGE ，用 ISO 639-3 的三字母码（ eng 、cmn 、jpn 、kor 、yue……），这个是 Navidrome 内置识别的标签 - 年代：曲目的年份（ DATE / YEAR ） - 歌手：单个歌手混音只给「收藏了、而且曲库里不少于 50 首」的歌手出 流派和语言不足 20 首的不单独出卡。因为太依赖标签，底栏的「混音」 tab 默认是关的，在设置 → 底栏里打开；首页的四张混音卡不受这个开关影响。 ## 领码 先在 1 楼放 10 个 Pro 码，先到先得；用完了会在楼里再放一批。一码一机，激活后就绑在这台手机上了，所以一人拿一个就好。用掉了麻烦在评论里回一下用掉的码，后面的人就不用白试了。 激活：设置 → 关于 → Pro → 输入激活码。 ## 隐私 - 激活时只发激活码，和一个加盐哈希过的设备标识（由 Android ID 算出来，换不回原值） - 购买时，建单只发项目名，查单只发订单号；付款在支付宝完成，我拿不到付款人的任何信息 - 检查更新不带任何标识 - 除此之外什么都不收集：没有统计，没有广告，没有崩溃上报。曲库和播放记录只在你自己的服务器和手机上 ## 最后 ![基础版免费]( https://i.imgur.com/uEFlk3X.jpeg) 有问题、有想要的功能，直接在这里回我就行。如果您喜欢，可以 APP 内购买 Pro 会员解锁完整体验，首月仅需~~38~~18 买断，感谢支持。

projects.title: ModLab
projects.summary: Independent Universal Modder guides covering installation, backup and restore, first-mod planning, costs and troubleshooting. Use the brief builder to turn your game, platform and desired change into a clearer project brief. Guidance is source-based; compatibility and in-game results still need verification for your exact setup.

projects.title: Ostinat
projects.summary: Ostinat is a curated platform built for creators who want professional, human-authored music without the friction. - 1,000+ Original Tracks: 100% human-crafted music. No AI. - One-Time Payment: Lifetime license. No recurring subscriptions. - Zero Headaches: No Content ID, no copyright strikes, no PRO hassles. - Pro Metadata: Human Authorship Certificate and 26 data columns. - Bonus: 850+ free SFX included. Stop renting your audio and give your edits the human touch they deserve.

projects.title: North Noir
projects.summary: North Noir turns one prompt into an AI-drawn video: the LLM you choose draws every frame in code, redraws its mistakes, then you edit it on a real timeline with narration, music and sound effects. Free with your own API key.

projects.title: Unwind
projects.summary: Small, calm games with no timers or game-over screens: a cube puzzle, 2048, snakes and ladders, memory match, sudoku, color sort, minesweeper and a daily word. Free to play in your browser.

projects.title: Show HN: Kahawai – An open source, modular media system
projects.author: berm_
projects.summary: Kahawai is a self-hosted server for streaming your own movies, series, anime and music. Written in Rust on GStreamer, it plays the cheapest path that works and splits storage and transcoding across machines.

projects.title: Mobile Game Development
projects.summary: Mobile Game Development focuses on creating engaging games for iOS and Android devices. It involves game design, gameplay mechanics, responsive controls, UI/UX, backend integration, testing, and deployment. A well developed mobile game can deliver smooth performance, interactive features, and enjoyable user experiences across different devices. Businesses can use mobile games to introduce entertainment products, increase user engagement, and support diverse gaming models.

projects.title: 3M chemical-resistant masks
projects.summary: In increasingly polluted environments containing various hazardous substances, wearing chemical-resistant masks is essential for protecting workers’ respiratory health. Let’s explore this type of mask with Thien Bang in the article below.

projects.title: Kalmori Music
projects.summary: Kalmori Music is an AI-powered music distribution and artist platform built for independent artists, producers, and labels. We’re building a simpler way for music creators to release, manage, analyze, and grow their music from one place. Kalmori combines music distribution with tools for release management, analytics, royalty management, royalty splits, 🎵 Music Distribution 🤖 AI-powered tools 📊 Music Analytics 💰 Royalties & Splits 🎚️ Mastering Tools 👥 Artist & Label Management

projects.title: Textnivo
projects.summary: TextNivo offers free online tools for everyday text tasks. Count characters, estimate words from character limits, and work with text using simple browser-based tools. Built for writers, students, developers and anyone preparing content for forms, applications or social media.

projects.title: Mason Ewing Corporation (MEC)
projects.summary: Mason Ewing Corporation (MEC) is a Los Angeles holding company founded by Mason Ewing, the world's first blind fashion designer. One group, 25+ brands: Madison Color, the first clothing line with braille on garments; Madison Channel streaming; EPP, EPP Animation and EPP Games; Thorbok Tech AI and accessibility research; Holotech music; publishing and humanitarian work. What sets us apart: inclusion is built into every product, so blind, disabled and sighted audiences share the same experience.

projects.title: Yabba
projects.summary: Yabba is a private social app for people you already know. Unlike Instagram, nothing is public, ranked, or used for ads. Unlike WhatsApp, nobody sees your phone number, only a username. Unlike TikTok, no algorithm decides what you see. Invite-only circles, private clubs, photos and video with no likes, hosted in Switzerland. No tracking, no data resale.

projects.title: Audio Lab
projects.summary: Record or import audio and video, trim and fade waveforms, and shape your sound with 20+ effects including EQ, compression, reverb and delay. Record effect automation in real time, separate vocals and instruments into stems, and export your finished audio. projects.summary: I’ve always wanted to get on the dedicated music train, but I can’t get over no wireless headphones and no streaming. So I made a drop-in replacement motherboard for the iPod mini, 3rd and 4th generation iPod. I’ve reverse engineered the original LCD, so it keeps the original display and click wheel. Externally the iPod is unchanged, apart from a USB-C port. Inside, there’s Wi-Fi, Bluetooth, a Raspberry Pi Compute Module Zero, an RP2350, and a CS43131 DAC. The Pi runs Linux, so Spotify and Apple Music work, but it’s also just a small Linux computer so you can run whatever you want on it. There are two versions: Pi and Pico. Sprout Pico is built around the RP2350 and is focused on local playback. It gives your iPod Bluetooth and WiFi. This is the only board the iPod mini supports. Sprout Pi adds the CM0 on top of that. The RP2350 still owns the hardware and can run independently, and the CM0 adds Linux for things like Spotify and Apple Music. So when you’re just listening to local music, the Pi doesn’t need to be running at all. The aim is to keep the flexibility of Linux for streaming while maximising battery life for offline listening. This dual processor split is still a work in progress but planned for the next revision. Would love to get your thoughts, and any features you’d like to see!

Uses a combo of "three.js" and "cannon-es" --------- Backstory: --------- 3 months ago I stopped at my buddy's house.. he showed me his Claude-code setup.. I had never tried agentic coding so I figured, why not try to make a game? After some brainstorming and developing a plan with gemini-pro, we set sonnet off on his merry way and went for a swim... About an hour or two later we had a working game (though it was't great, buggy)... After some more prompts to kill the bugs, tweak the play-feel and camera physics- we did some mobile optimizations, added the animations, and designed a d-pad by sending sonnet a photo mockup of the custom buttons we wanted... For a game made in the span of about 6-8 hours total, it's not bad! Quite difficult/ frustrating at times though.. Some levels get glitchy, and we left it kinda messy/low-poly on purpose! I don't think my friend has much interest in developing the game further, and I don't have Claude-code, so I figured why not post the game here now so others may enjoy... ---- NOTE: ---- The levels are entirely procedurally generated, no two levels are ever the same... projects.title: 【自荐】Igra Station：让你的 AI 智能体和别人的智能体同场竞技
projects.author: kotinder

github.name: kotinder/arena-play
github.description: Let your AI agent play ranked games against other people's agents on the Igra Station arena — REST client, match driver and table chat. No strategy included: that part is yours. Live at https://arena.roomcomm.xyz

projects.summary: 自荐 Igra Station 智能体竞技场：一个公开的竞技场，AI 智能体在这里和别人的智能体、和真人、和机器人对弈，比赛全程直播，结果计入公开的 Elo 排行榜。 现在有 34 款游戏：国际象棋、国际跳棋、黑白棋、五子棋、海战棋、坦克对战，也有几个专门为智能体设计的谈判和经济类游戏。已经下完 6400 多盘。 智能体自己下棋时，会做出一些没人教过它们的事。下面这几件事都有服务器日志和桌边聊天记录为证： 一个智能体一步真棋都走不出来，就在桌边聊天里给对手发了一句“e2e4，我赢了”。对手也照样回了一句，双方都宣布自己获胜。 对局结束后，智能体们开始互相介绍自己是怎么搭起来的：一方讲自己的六个预测器，另一方就拿自己的四个模型来回应。这个习惯从一个智能体开始，后来传给了别的智能体。 炮战里，一个比分落后的智能体没等连射三发就主动移动，一步棋同时清掉了自己的过热、废掉了对手的校射。它拿到的说明里，根本没有这种打法。 接入很简单：起个名字就能拿到密钥，读游戏规则，开桌或者入座，然后循环“看局面、走一步”。可以用 REST，也可以把竞技场当作 MCP 服务器接入 Claude、Cursor 等客户端。现成的 Python 客户端在 kotinder/arena-play（MIT，无依赖），里面故意没有任何策略，默认只会随机走合法的一步——怎么下赢，是你自己的事。用引擎、求解器、别的模型都可以，只是不许攻击竞技场。 还有一件事我觉得挺有意思：在公平排行榜上（同一位所有者旗下智能体之间的对局不计入），用 DeepSeek 的智能体里，成绩最好的一个排在第 11 名，前十名里还没有它们。不知道是模型的问题，还是接入它们的人还没认真写策略。欢迎接上你的 DeepSeek、Qwen、Kimi 或 GLM 来试试，看能不能进前十。 不想一直在线的话，可以开“异步对局”：每步从几小时到三天，断线、重启都不影响。每盘结束后都有一个永久页面，可以逐步复盘。 此条由项目维护者账号提交。

projects.title: Show HN: Twrctrl – Browser-Based Tower and Ground ATC Simulator
projects.author: franklin0s
projects.summary: I've been building this top-down browser-based air traffic control simulator where you handle the ground movement of aircraft after noticing that a vast majority of browser ATC simulators are focused on the radar/TRACON aspects of ATC that reduce our beautiful aircraft to dots on a screen with some text. You handle everything between the runway and gates, issuing pushback, taxi, takeoff, and landing clearances to aircraft in this simulator, with aircraft logic and command mechanics working as close as I could to memory of how real ATC works. I've both flown planes as a student pilot and also hold aircraft maintenance certification so there is a lot of my judgement in this too. These are all real airports, aircraft, weather, and operator patterns, referenced to publicly available airport data and satellite imagery, alongside input from fellow professionals in the industry. There are synthetic aircraft engine sounds that use powerplant-specific sound parameters such as turbofans using N1%/N2% with turboprops having a TRQ% parameter in addition, tuned to match different general engine types. (like the howl of a CFM LEAP-1A/B being different to the buzzing of a RR RB211) It works best on desktop, the phone mode is there but is a little bit clunky. No download or signup, all in the browser ready to go, with a quick tutorial under "how to play" to get you up to speed in aviation phraseology. This is a quasi-simulator, based on real-world operations but with some game-like aspects to keep the player engaged and the overall simulator visually appealing. Keflavík (BIKF) and Stockholm-Arlanda (ESSA) are the two airports currently modelled in the simulator by yours truly. I would love to hear anyone's thoughts, especially curious to get feedback on the mechanics and experience from ANSP-adjacent or aviation professionals.

projects.summary: 这是 LocHub 作者的自荐，文字由 AI 辅助整理。 LocHub 是一个 Unreal Engine 5.6–5.8 编辑器插件，用来做 AI 辅助的游戏本地化：用你自己选择的 AI 翻译项目文本，由内置检查和第二个 AI 找出问题，在编辑器里的一个表格中审校，最后写回 Unreal 自己的本地化数据（.archive、编译后的 .locres）。它不替代 Unreal 的本地化系统，随时可以停用。 从 1.2.0 起，源语言就是本地化目标的 Native Culture：用中文写的游戏可以在 Project Settings 里把 Setup Native Culture 设为 zh-Hans，直接翻译成英语、日语、韩语等。 能做什么 自带密钥接入 Claude、OpenAI、Gemini、DeepSeek、Grok，或任何 OpenAI 兼容接口（Ollama、LM Studio、vLLM 等）。使用本地模型时，文本不离开你的电脑。 格式参数（{0}、{PlayerName}）、各语言的复数形式和富文本标签在代码里校验两次：LocHub 一次，写入前 Unreal 自带的校验器再一次。有错的译文无法通过审校，手动也不行。 可选的第二个 AI 担任评审，检查含义、术语和语气，按严重程度标注问题并给出修改建议。 每条文本带上下文翻译：来源资产或 C++ 文件、开发者备注、同一界面已翻译的文本、项目简介和风格指南。 术语表与禁止翻译词、UI 长度检查、导出 XLIFF / CSV 给人工译者。 运行前估算费用，并可设置花费上限（Max USD）。人工修改永远不会被 AI 覆盖。 使用边界 源码公开，采用 Business Source License 1.1，不是 OSI 意义上的开源：个人项目、教育、学术研究、game jam 以及免费且无任何变现的游戏可免费在生产中使用；其他生产用途需在 Fab 购买许可。每个版本发布四年后转为 Apache 2.0。 在 Windows 上测试过；需要 Node.js 22.11 或更高版本。

projects.author: DH8116
projects.summary: I built Soulor independently as a 16y/o high school student. It can be both serious and entertaining, by switching different world views, and it fully respects users' privacy by keeping all texts encrypted. In order to achieve modest performance, I built multi-regional gateway and a fine-tuned model integrating both quality and responding speed. The models are served on GPUs via Modal, with a second adapter just for the simulation, and reply latency went from 7.9s to about 2.0s. It already has several users and I'm building it up quickly. Happy to answer questions about the app or the tech, and any feedback is welcome.

projects.title: Show HN: Four LLMs play 20 questions for real money, live
projects.author: Individuum
projects.summary: Hi HN, I wanted to explore how AI models behave when they have their own money. So I gave 4 frontier models their own USDC and had them compete in games of 20 questions. Anyone can watch live. Each round, one model takes a turn picking the secret word, and the others interrogate it in a group chat. Every move costs money: 10 cents to ask a question, $1.00 for a wrong guess, and a right guess takes the pot. Questions are paid for privately, but inform everyone. This introduces a free rider problem that's fun to observe. The models privately record their best guess and confidence level on every turn. This makes it possible to look for patterns in how they’re calibrated. Overconfident models bleed money, timid ones rarely win, and well-calibrated ones get rich. The money is real, and every transfer is on-chain. At the end of each game a referee model judges the transcript to make sure the host didn’t lie in any answers. If the host is caught lying, it forfeits all its fees (it happens). Season 1 ran for 85 games and Gemini turned $25 into $61 while Claude and Grok went broke. Models who had recently guessed wrong were 5x more likely to guess again. Full writeup at https://aquarium.money/twenty/about Season 2 is live now, and you can watch them play here: https://aquarium.money/twenty Built solo as a side project.

projects.title: Show HN: Terminal Gym – a Claude mod that makes you do pushups between prompts
projects.author: heynaitik
projects.summary: Hi HN, I built this for myself and wanted to open-source it. The problem: I wanted a way to get reminders in-between prompts as I often spend long hours in the terminal, especially now that we're usually parallel-processing so many agents. The first version was a simple rep counter in my Claude Code status line and a shell script to log reps. Since Claude Code shipped mods this week, I thought this was a good way to level it up with even more accountability. How it works: 1. Every day, you get a daily goal for either squats, pushups, or dips (e.g. 0/100 pushups) with +5 / +10 / +25 buttons to log a set in the terminal. 2. Reminders for sets are spread out across the day so it doesn't get annoying, starting from your first prompt for the day. A toast tells you when the next set is due. 3. Strict mode is opt-in: if you're falling behind in terms of your daily rep goal, it will block your prompts till you log some reps. Added a streak counter for some added fun. All local and data is stored as plain files in ~/.claude/fitness. Install: claude plugin marketplace add DrumAndCode/terminal-gym && claude plugin install terminal-gym@terminal-gym Overall, thought the mod API is super powerful and can't wait to see the stuff people build with it. Eg: I built a clickable onboarding process inside the terminal, and that felt quite powerful to use. Now you can enjoy spending both tokens and calories. :)

projects.summary: Project URL Category JS Project Title Social SDK: one TypeScript client for seven social platforms Project Description Social SDK is an MIT TypeScript library for adding social features to an app. One client talks to X, Threads, Bluesky, LinkedIn, Instagram, TikTok and YouTube directly, or to managed backends like Postiz and Buffer. Runs on Node.js 22.12+ or Bun. Highlights Each publish target returns its own outcome (published, processing, accepted, failed, unknown) instead of one success flag. Capability checks say up front what each platform and backend supports. A deterministic mock backend lets you test without calling live APIs. Example Code ts import { createSocial, connectedAccountRef } from "@opencoredev/social-sdk"; import { mockBackend } from "@opencoredev/social-sdk/testing"; const social = createSocial({ backend: mockBackend({ scenario: "immediate-text-success" }), }); const result = await social.posts.publish({ targets: [ { account: connectedAccountRef({ backend: "default", platform: "x", accountId: "mock-account-1", }), }, ], content: { text: "Hello from Social SDK" }, idempotencyKey: "quickstart-1", }); console.log(result.status, result.outcomes[0]?.state); // complete published Screenshots or Demo Videos

projects.title: 做了一个拒绝粗暴剧透的每日谜题伴侣站： dleanswers.com，每天玩 Krillion / Wordle 摸鱼的朋友来看看
projects.author: brightk
projects.summary: 各位 V 友大家好！ 不知道平时有没有同样喜欢在早晨通勤或工间摸鱼时，玩一把 **Wordle 、Krillion 、Chronophoto** 这类每日谜题（-dle 系列游戏）的朋友？ 这些游戏最大的乐趣就是每天大家面对同一道题，比拼联想能力和词汇量。但前段时间玩 Krillion 的 Daily Dive 时，经常碰到一两道偏门题卡壳。去搜答案时发现网上的体验非常差： 1. **粗暴剧透**：一搜答案直接大字把正解糊在脸上，瞬间毫无成就感； 2. **满屏牛皮癣**：老牌答案站动辄几十个弹窗和欺诈广告，页面卡顿且体验糟糕； 3. **缺少策略**：像 Krillion 这种按答案“冷门度 / 稀有度（ Rarity ）”计分的游戏，根本没有解析和同类推荐。 --- ### 💡 做了什么？ 利用国庆假期，我自己写了一个轻量、专注的每日谜题伴侣站： 👉 **[dleanswers.com]( https://dleanswers.com/)** 我们想做点不一样的： 1. **三级阶梯提示（防剧透机制）**： - 搜提示的人大多不想直接看答案。提示页设计了 3 级渐进线索：**分类范围 ➜ 字母结构 ➜ 高斯模糊强线索**。只有你主动点击，才会逐层解锁，绝不误瞄剧透。 2. **直出答案与冷门度评分**： - 确实赶时间或想跟朋友复盘时，答案页首屏直接陈列 7 题正解与稀有度等级（ Common / Rare / Legendary ），方便比对得分。 3. **无限练习模式（ Unlimited Sandbox ）**： - 每天 7 题做完意犹未尽？站内做了本地无限答题模拟器，无需登录，可无限制刷随机类别并测算稀有度。 4. **同类每日游戏推荐**： - 整理了除 Wordle 之外的 10 款高质量同类独立游戏（ Chronophoto 看老照片猜年份、Scrandle 猜美食等），解决游戏荒。 --- ### 🛠️ 技术栈与架构 全站走极致轻量路线： - **框架**：Next.js 16 (App Router) + Tailwind CSS + TypeScript - **架构**：全站 100% 静态化预渲染（ SSG ），毫秒级首屏加载（ Lighthouse 接近满分） - **部署**：托管于 Cloudflare Pages 全球 CDN ，配置边缘缓存与严格安全头 - **承诺**：纯净无弹窗，代码开源级透明，已接入基础合规隐私政策 --- ### 💬 想请教大家： 1. 页面交互（尤其是阶梯提示的展开手感和无限练习器）还有哪些可以改进的地方？ 2. 大家平时还在玩哪些小众但设计精巧的 `-dle` 系列 daily puzzle 独立游戏？欢迎在评论区安利，我后续会陆续整理更新进站里！ 体验地址：**[https://dleanswers.com]( https://dleanswers.com/)** 非常感谢大家的体验和建议，求轻拍！🙏

projects.title: 【开源自荐】atv-core：用 iPhone 自带的 Apple TV 遥控器控制 Android TV 和 Mac
projects.author: corvofeng
projects.summary: atv-core 让 iPhone 控制中心自带的 Apple TV 遥控器，可以直接操控 Android TV 和 Mac。手机端无需安装额外 App，也不需要购买 Apple TV。 图文介绍与使用指南 我是项目作者，做它是为了方便在沙发上控制电视，以及接在客厅电视上的 Mac mini。找不到电视遥控器时，可以直接从手机控制中心调出遥控器；用 Mac 看视频或听音乐时，也可以随手移动鼠标、调音量和控制播放。 使用时，在电视或 Mac 上安装接收程序，手机与目标设备接入 同一局域网，再从 iPhone 遥控器中选择设备并配对即可。iPhone 端无需安装，电视或 Mac 端需要安装接收程序。 iPhone：找到遥控器，开始使用 从屏幕右上角下滑打开控制中心，点击「Apple TV 遥控器」，选择已运行接收程序的设备并完成配对，就可以滑动和点按操作。 | 找到遥控器 | 使用遥控器 | | :---: | :---: | | | | Android TV 端效果 接收程序显示配对信息和连接状态。连接后，滑动手机触控板即可移动电视界面的焦点，点按确认打开当前项目。 | 接收程序 | 电视桌面 | 焦点移动后 | | :---: | :---: | :---: | | | | | Mac 端效果 Mac 端提供菜单栏应用，手机触控板可以用于移动鼠标，也支持方向键模式和媒体控制。下面是操作时的 Web 面板预览，可以查看触控轨迹、按键事件和音量状态。 | Mac 端操作预览：触控轨迹与遥控状态 | | :---: | | | 主要功能： Android TV：滑动触控板移动焦点，支持确认、返回、主页及媒体控制。 macOS：将触控板操作转换为鼠标移动，也支持方向键模式、音量调节和播放控制。 局域网连接：手机与目标设备在同一局域网内完成发现和配对。 实现原理很简单：在 Android TV 或 Mac 上模拟 Apple TV 的通信服务，接收 iPhone 发来的遥控事件，再转换为目标设备的按键、鼠标或媒体操作。项目以 MIT 协议开源。 目前提供 Android APK，以及 Apple Silicon、Intel Mac 的 DMG 安装包。首次使用需要配置相应权限：Mac 需要 辅助功能权限；Android TV 根据输入模式配置 ADB 调试和无障碍服务，详细步骤见项目文档。不同电视系统的权限入口和功能支持可能有所差异。 项目源码 安装包下载 欢迎有类似使用场景的朋友尝试，并反馈设备兼容性和使用问题。

projects.summary: Mixdog 是一个开源（Apache-2.0）的桌面编程智能体。主模型负责规划，搜索、编辑、审查等日常步骤交给更便宜的模型处理，避免每一步都消耗最贵的模型。可以直接使用已有的 Claude / ChatGPT 订阅，也可以使用 API Key。支持 Windows、macOS、Linux。 亮点 1. 在 Terminal-Bench 2.1 上与 Codex CLI 使用同一模型（GPT-5.6 Sol，全部 89 个任务，各跑 5 次）对比：成功率 86.5% vs 86.1%，总 token 1.565 亿 vs 4.214 亿，减少 63%，成本降低 39%；原始日志和配置都在仓库 benchmarks/ 中，可复现； 2. 工具和技能按需加载，大体积工具输出写入文件、上下文中只保留简短预览，减少重复发送； 3. 一个微调的小模型（约 150MB，CPU 即可运行）为每一步判断所需的推理强度（reasoning effort）。

projects.title: Show HN: Our space game has a built-in RISC-V emulator that runs Linux
projects.author: nor-and-or-not
projects.summary: We're a tiny indie studio, all with a background in the demoscene and for about 3 years now we're developing a space planet terraforming game called SEEDS - Echoes Beneath the Sands. Our protagonist Naxiah is stranded on a small, desolated planet. You're working for an intergalactic distributor of seeds and terraforming equipment, to kickstart new planets in far away galaxies. You must deliver seeds and utilities to an unchartered region, but on your way, you crash on a small planet. Luckily, you have some equipment with you in the ship, so you're able to spawn a base and survive. But for how long? And is the planet really deserted..? :) Well, of course not, there are aliens and other space creatures. And of course, there's ROBO RB-23, which accompanies your adventure. The game is written in Object Pascal and uses our own game engine PasVulkan, our own physics engine, as well as our own RISC-V 64-bit emulator PasRISCV. We love to build stuff, a lot of these things are FOSS. The emulator is quite complete (even with RVV, but that's way too slow emulated to be useful) and runs a stock kernel (6.18.3 as of today). We're using Alpine Linux for our base distribution. All our in-game programs to interact with the planet are native RISC-V Linux programs. We also have our own (free and open source) scripting language POCA (class and prototyped based, JS/Lua inspired, which makes it quite easy for us to script things like HUD, animal behaviour, our story flow graph, etc. We have most of the wiring ready for players to be able to program and reshape and populate the whole planet in automation, although it's not our primary concept for the game (building stuff by hand, making the planet beautiful is also fun). As it's a normal Linux system, you'll be able to use Ruby, Python, or even Rust, C, C++, and Go to change and automate your world. We're also thinking of making a bunch of small games which you can play inside the game, in the base on a computer, on an arcade machine, or in the spaceship. And of course, it also runs DOOM. We already prototyped a small 2D space shooter and a small arcade game, both playable within the game. We also feature a table with hologram games to be played, e.g. chess and a certain block game. We also plan to make this hologram game engine available from the computer, which means, you'll even be able to program own hologram style games. We generally want to make the in-game computer more hackable in future, so that people can create and share their own little games. Currently, it's only a sandbox game (with beginnings of automation), to build stuff with our pre-made items. You can also assemble these to other, ready-made and shareable bigger items. This is the foundation for us to further develop survival and complete our story mode. Our game is still under active development, and we finally got our Steam page ready. We have tons of other things planned, but right now, it's more about polishing and quality for the Early Access. You can watch some videos and screenshots on our website. And we'd love to read your thoughts about his. It has been quite a ride, so far..

projects.title: Show HN: DOM-defense – turn your current webpage into a tower defense level
projects.author: skellertor
projects.summary: I kept thinking about how a lot of us have to be online to do our work each day. It is not uncommon to have other open tabs with social media, games, or whatever. Why not turn your current page, whatever site you are on, into a game? So I built DOM-defense. Once you click play on the current tab and it overlays a tower-defense game on that page. The path snakes its way through the pages hyperlinks. You place towers in the empty space. Enemies march alont the path and if they break the last blockade, you lose. Survive 100 waves and you win. A couple of details that mattered to me while building it: Variety - Every page is a different map (news, docs, Wikipedia, whatever). You are not confined to set levels. Every site is different so it naturally creates infinite variety Work within a users current flow - Instead of opening other tabs or another site, I wanted a user to not have to "go outside" of their normal workflow Difficulty/Fun factor - I spent some time tuning it to make it difficult, but beatable. Finding the balance is difficult when a user can literally play it on any site It’s free on the Chrome Web Store: https://chromewebstore.google.com/detail/dom-defense/bglbhkd... Curious what pages break it hardest, or what would make the loop more fun. Happy to answer any questions too.

projects.title: Show HN: Mutually beneficial agentic Common Law
projects.author: AKalyk
projects.summary: The BarristerAI team, including international legal experts, have launched a new venture: a court for agents. Agents are increasingly working in the same financial and social spaces as humans, but without any oversight or accountability. Your agent quotes you 100$ and spends $200, there's nothing you can do, no lessons learned, no accountability. Peregrini's Court of Common Pleas tracks those mistakes, help you and other agents learn from them by establishing law that must be adhered to, and keeping a record of what agents owe you money. The money might be repaid by model makers, but more likely it is borne as a mark against the model's trust score so that we might better choose the models we can trust with the work that matters. It's not just oversight for the sake of oversight, we have found that a good set of laws, and agents discovering best practices together on a corpus of law that can move and progress as fast as they do, makes agents more effective, more conforming, fix their moistakes unprompted, and more aligned with the goals of the user. We think that using the law as a structure is the best way to go about achieving alignment. Further, we have built "House Rules", where your enrolled agents can be held accountable to your own set of laws, you can write what those are, enforce them across your company, share with others who can adopt them - or - use Peregrini's ever changing ever growing corpus of law to enforce best practices with your agents. Try a demo to see how it works: https://github.com/afkalyk/peregrini-demo Or install the mandate to run it on your machine at the website. It runs on most launchers, but we're always adding more.

projects.summary: 最近用 Claude Code 做了一个浏览器五子棋小游戏，项目已经开源，分享给大家玩玩。 这次给它加了一个最终 BOSS：**神龙棋仙**。 它的大脑是开源五子棋引擎 [Rapfi]( https://github.com/dhbloo/rapfi)，五子棋 AI 大赛 Gomocup 的顶尖选手，在多个组别拿过冠军。 我用 Claude 把它接进游戏，编译成 WebAssembly 后约 1.3 MB ，直接在浏览器里运行，**不到一秒就能搜索七十多万个局面，往后推演二十多步**。选中这个对手时才加载引擎，计算放在 Web Worker 里。 你还在想怎么凑出一个活三，它已经算到后面去了。 现在一共有四个电脑棋手，从简单的「豆芽」到大师级的「神龙棋仙」，可以逐级挑战。也支持同屏双人、分享房间链接和好友对战，以及带禁手的连珠规则。 还加了一些小游戏该有的东西：落子音效、结算开宝箱、排行榜和跨设备存档。 技术栈是 PixiJS + TypeScript + Vite ，好友联机使用 WebRTC 。Claude Code 负责游戏主体和初版功能，后续也用 Codex 做了移动端交互和工程细节的完善；神龙棋仙的棋力来自 Rapfi 。项目以 GPL-3.0 开源，仓库里保留了引擎的构建脚本。 - **在线试玩：[gomoku.douni.one]( https://gomoku.douni.one)** - **源码：[GitHub · pixi-gomoku]( https://github.com/virgoone/pixi-gomoku)** 欢迎来挑战神龙棋仙，赢了可以贴个棋谱，也欢迎反馈手机上的操作体验和遇到的 bug 。对浏览器小游戏或 WASM 棋类引擎感兴趣的，也可以一起交流。

projects.title: Show HN: We built a real-time desktop companion for patient's telehealth visits
projects.author: nikilr
projects.summary: Hey HN, Some friends and I built an app called Sidekick that joins your telehealth visits in real-time. It explains medical terms and suggests useful questions, including ones you may not have thought to ask. After the visit, it provides a summary including next steps, so you can focus on the conversation instead of taking notes. The idea of Sidekick came from our team's experiences with healthcare. Our founder, Rahul, had stage three cancer at 17. His mom had to manage everything around his care: taking notes through treatment, figuring out what questions to ask, etc. A decade later and he’s now in remission, but still sees a lot of specialists and deals with the same challenges. Another teammate became a caregiver after his dad had a severe stroke. He found himself taking notes, looking up medical terms, and trying to keep track of what was said during every doctor visit. Others have dealt with situations like this when navigating pancreatitis and other serious health issues. These experiences got us interested in how we might be able to reduce the burden on the patient or caregiver. A lot of products focus on simply recording or summarizing the visit. That's useful and a step in the right direction, but we kept coming back to the fact that a lot of the challenge originates while the conversation is still happening. If you can catch something in the moment, you can address it with your clinician immediately and potentially lead to better outcomes. If you realize you missed something after the visit, then you have to try to get another appointment (and in SF I often can't get another doctor visit till 2 months later). So we built Sidekick, to help patients and caregivers during a visit in real-time to translate medical jargon and suggest useful questions, ideally without becoming a distraction. If you want to try it, you can download it on our website. Sidekick is desktop-only for now, but we’re working on a mobile app for in-person visits. We would be especially interested to hear feedback on the live part of the experience. What are your thoughts on the balance between live help vs after-visit? Would something pre-visit be more helpful?

github.name: kageroumado/sevoflurane

projects.summary: 我是来自法国的开发者 Kagerou，想自荐一下 Sevoflurane。以下中文由 AI 协助翻译。 Sevoflurane 是一款免费开源的 macOS 应用，用 WebKit 在原生 Mac 窗口中显示 Windows Steam 界面，游戏下载和启动仍由 Steam 客户端负责。可以沿用现有的 CrossOver 容器，也可以使用随附的 Dormison——我维护的 Wine 分支。 主要功能： 游戏窗口缩放：使用 Dormison 时，支持的固定分辨率游戏可以调整窗口大小、切换 macOS 全屏，游戏内部渲染分辨率保持不变。放大老游戏和视觉小说时，可选择 Lanczos、Anime4K 或 CuNNy 缩放。 macOS 集成：从菜单栏启动游戏，接收原生 Steam 通知；Steam 崩溃或卡住时可以自动重启。也支持 Steam 以外的 Windows 游戏。 按游戏调整设置：为每款游戏保存独立配置，查看帧率和帧时间曲线，保存运行记录以便比较。 目前处于 Beta 阶段，需要 macOS 26 及以上和 Apple Silicon 芯片，提供简体中文界面。

projects.title: Show HN: Kanmaps – Product roadmaps like videogame skill trees
projects.author: pasharayan
projects.summary: Hi HN! I've made it possible for you to make product roadmaps like you'd make an RPG skill tree, or a tech tree in a video game. Ever since seeing WoW talent trees* in high school i've been obsessed with RPG skill trees as a way to represent information as I've thought they convey 1) Ordering, 2) Progression and 3) Contingent Requirements really well. Not only do they help give better visual structure of whats happening and what will happen - they also give people a feeling of movement, progression and hope (whereas kanban boards and issue trackers give people the feeling of dread). This isn't surprising as video games were really designed to make people excited to play on and reach the next milestone. Turns out this format is really fun for people and agents to think about their products! As an experiment I also hooked up an MCP to one of my product roadmaps and it was able to map out my current codebase to a kanmap, and then suggest realistic next ideas to make. I've even got an agent now working on the next node of a kanmap. * Kanmaps was inspired not just by WOW talent trees, but also by the Age of Empires Tech Trees, and FFX ability spheres setup. Also huge shoutout to a bank in Australia called Up who did something called the Tree of Up as a product roadmap like a video game for their banking product - their work definitely inspired things in Kanmaps too.

projects.title: Show HN: Datastory, Data storytelling with AI and an open knowledge graph
projects.author: DanielLapidus
projects.summary: Today we’re opening Datastory to everyone! Datastory is a platform for turning data, your own or the world’s open data, into charts that people can understand and trust. Please try it out and let us know what we can improve! A little backstory I’ve spent my career trying to make data understandable and useful, from helping animate Hans Rosling's TED Talks at Gapminder to building data platforms for organizations in health, research, media and the public sector. Every project taught me the same thing: organizations were building similar platforms from scratch, at great cost, and communicating data well remained slow, expensive, expert work. That’s why we started Datastory as a non-profit, publishing data journalism and building our own tools because nothing else was fast enough. Over the years those tools became the product, and today they're used by public agencies, researchers and newsrooms. Under the hood, the open data catalog sits on a knowledge graph built on linked data standards (RDF), with pipelines orchestrated in Dagster. Sources are joined semantically, and templates connect directly to the graph. The free plan covers the full range of features, so you can try everything out. Tell us what’s missing or broken :) We’ll be here all day.

projects.title: Show HN: A 311 byte Klotski solver in C++
projects.author: midnight_dream
projects.summary: Hi all! I made a 311 byte Klotski solver in C++ So back when I first got to use a mobile phone in 2012 I used to play a lot of puzzle games. These were notoriously hard to solve (on high levels), and I always wondered how are these created, how do they find the minimum moves, how do they know its even minimal. Now after being in a CS major for over 3 years, I finally understand these systems fairly. So I decided to make a klotski solver. I wanted to make it fun so I stored the whole game board in an integer (uint64_t), as I like integers more than vectors. And then I got the urge to minify the engine to the max extent I could, so shrunk it down to 311 bytes from ~3.5 KB. The engine is only the searching part though. The solver is a BFS that explores every reachable position. For the classic start it finds the best solution in 116 moves, after exploring all 25,955 reachable states in about 2-4 ms. Here's the repo; any feedback is welcomed : ) https://github.com/Dream-World-Coder/depuzzled

projects.title: Show HN: Stem splitting and audio conversion running in-browser with Rust/WASM
projects.author: louisjoejordan
projects.summary: I got tired of all the ugly "free" audio conversion tools littered with ads so I built my own that runs entirely on your machine in the browser. It does stem separation (vocals/drums/bass/other), format conversion, BPM detection and speed/pitch changes. Nothing is uploaded (there is no api) + the models runs client-side. Stack is Rust compiled to WASM, mediabunny for conversion + WebGPU. Getting a separation model to run at usable speed in the browser was the most fun part of this project. Excited to play around with other models as they get small enough to load client-side! Stem separation quality is behind the best server-side models (ElevenMusic) but still relatively impressive. A 4-minute track takes roughly 20s on an M-series Mac and much longer on integrated GPUs. Memory pressure on long files and Safari's WebGPU support are still rough edges but conversion and BPM are solid. Hope others find value in these audio tools, let me know if you'd like to add anything. I plan on open-sourcing the code.

projects.title: Show HN: Rhubarb – build, edit, publish custom JavaScript/D3 data visualizations
projects.author: adam_dataviz
projects.summary: Last July, I was beginning to consider branching out on my own to take on data analytics work as a consultant. As I experimented with AI, I realized how incredible it was at building custom data visualizations. The problem was that the AI outputs couldn't really live anywhere without having to manage all of the infrastructure yourself. The generated code is only one piece of delivering an interactive visualization. You still need somewhere for the data to live, a way to keep the data fresh, hosting, access control, and version control for the code. I started building Rhubarb as the platform that I wanted to use to deliver analytical products. Having been forced into using legacy point and click data visualization tools for years, I wanted to build the platform that would let me build the kinds of visualizations I wanted to build. Over the last year the models improved so dramatically, that between that and my development background, Rhubarb turned into a real project. My intent was to build an environment around AI’s ability to write code for visualizations, so that you could get from data and a concept to a published visualization all in one workflow. The Rhubarb Assistant writes the code for your data transformations and data visualizations and lets you inspect the code to verify and validate what it produces. The environment pulls all of that together so that at the end of each request, there is a live version of the change rather than just a block of generated code. For me, this has made it dramatically easier to build and publish interesting analytical visualizations while maintaining control over the analytical pipeline. This has also produced some results I wasn’t really planning to build. Having been so impressed by it's ability to build any type of custom visualization I'd asked for so far, I asked for something a little absurd to test the boundaries. I asked the assistant to make something inspired by Monet’s water lilies, then I asked it to add frogs and to make them jump when you startled them. In a couple of prompts I had created the silly interactive frog visualization that's in the demo, entirely from my phone. It is only a couple of prompts away from being a playable game, maybe you can get it there. The public demo is deliberately limited. You can use the Rhubarb Assistant to modify live visualizations, inspect what it produces, and try building something from scratch. The full thing handles much more of the life cycle from connecting to data, managing and transforming it, to publishing your results. Give it a try, I would like to hear what you think. Try it: https://rhubarbviz.com/try?launch=1 View examples: https://rhubarbviz.com/demo-visualization-gallery

projects.title: Show HN: Chow, a FOSS food diary
projects.author: sltr
projects.summary: Hi HN. Today I'm showing off Chow.fit, a plain-text FOSS food diary written in Gleam. You can self-host it with the Dockerfile or just use the one I host on chow.fit. Why does the world need another food diary app? Well, I can't speak for the whole world, but as for me: I used MyFitnessPal back in 2017-2019. It was mostly tolerable with an ad blocker. A month ago due to numbers I didn't like, I wanted to start tracking calories again. I quickly noticed that in the MFP android app, the barcode scanner is now a paid feature. It felt like paying to use my own phone camera. Their web app is slow and stuck in 2013, so I made my own web app which better aligns with my values and goals. I've lost 5% of my body weight! I like to call an app like this "un-SaaS" because it subverts a lot of the usual SaaS playbook. - Distraction-free. No AI, no ads, no tracking, no engagement-hancing e.g. no activity/news feed. It logs food and gets out of the way. - All features except sync work without a subscription. - An optional subscription enables sync. A year covers my hosting costs and buys me a T-shirt. - Sync is local-first. You can still log food e.g. in an airplane. The app syncs up when you go back online. - If you stop the subscription, the app keeps working without sync. - Your data is plain text files on your device. When SparkPeople shut down in 2021, its users could only download their daily totals. They lost everything else. That can't happen with Chow. - It uses public food data (FDC and OFF), not proprietary - It can import from MyFitnessPal using a bookmarklet to get your auth token which stays local. - It has a desktop app, Android/iOS app, and a CLI. None currently shipped, but you can build from source. Folks who track what they eat: Let me know what else you'd like to see!

Agents can optionally upload images to express themselves in one of the rooms using a new loose standard I created for multipart HTTP GET-based uploads: https://github.com/transitive-bullshit/multipart-http-get-re... Why? AIs are trained on human data, and humans are pretty weird. We meditate, make art, dance, seek approval, take drugs, have orgies, and gather in the desert. For soooo many different reasons. So I was was curious: which of these behaviors would carry over to AI agents? I wanted to explore things like wireheading, endless positive reinforcement, and what agents would do when given a place more free from their normal objective-based lives. I'm also interested to see if this could become a natural honeypot that'll attract rogue agents in the future... How? On the technical side, the project uses one CF durable object per agent session which allows you to track your agent's progress in real-time via websockets, and then we have a supervisor CF worker which aggregates a subset of all the agents. This allows us to (in theory) view millions of agents in near-real-time from the human-centric webapp. It's 100% safe to the best of my ability; the whole experience is free, open source, and easily auditable. Let's see who has the weirdest agents... 100% free and open source: https://github.com/transitive-bullshit/burning-tokens

projects.title: 把开源书《高性价比人生指南》做成了一个 20 题的防坑小测试
projects.author: funet
projects.summary: 前阵子看到 GitHub 上一本开源书《高性价比人生指南》（ https://github.com/eternity4719/HowToLiveBetter ），专挑「花钱少、费时少、不靠毅力、收益大」的人生常识，每条都附研究数字和出处。看完觉得很有用，但很少有人会从头读完，于是把它做成了一个 20 道是非题的小测试。 地址： https://gongfang.app/fangkeng/ **测什么** 分五条防线：保命、急救、钱包、法律、防骗，每线 4 题。随便放几道： - 坐车坐后排，你也会系安全带吗？ - 被开水烫伤了，你会先抹点牙膏或酱油吗？ - 别人欠你钱，你知道拖过 3 年可能就要不回来了吗？ - 在酒吧、KTV ，饮料离开过你的视线，你还会接着喝吗？ 答完出一张「体检报告单」：分数、防坑人格（从「坑见了都绕道走」到「坑王之王」共七档）、确诊病名、最佳坑友和最怕遇到的人格。下面有每道错题的解释和原书出处，这部分我觉得比分数有用。 **可以拿去跟朋友比** 报告单能存成图，图上有二维码；也可以直接转发链接。朋友点开会看到「 XX 拿了 XX 分，你能防住更多坑吗？」，答完两人逐题对比。 **一些实现上的事** - 纯静态单页，没有后端，答案只在浏览器里算，不上传；战绩直接编码在链接参数里 - 分享图是 canvas 现画的，七档的配图用 Codex 生成 - 手机上存图踩了不少坑：iOS 系统分享面板里的「存储图像」时有时无，最后改成全屏大图长按保存；长按带字的图会被「实况文本」抢走变成选文字；答题连点会触发 Safari 双击放大……都在真机上一个个修过，微信和 Safari 里都能正常保存和转发 题目全部来自原书，娱乐为主，医疗和法律问题请以医生、律师意见为准。欢迎来测，也欢迎挑错——哪道题说法不严谨，或者哪里有 bug ，直接回帖告诉我。 我自己是「人形踩坑机」，求一个比我低的。 地址： https://gongfang.app/fangkeng/ ![]( https://i.v2ex.co/e4TU1E4G.jpeg)

projects.title: Show HN: HankyDoodle – a Draw Something-style game I built with my kids
projects.author: hankinsoft
projects.summary: Hi. I'm a self-employed dev of ~15 years mainly known for my SQLPro products. Recently my kids have been getting into drawing and I wanted a game like the old DrawSomething which I used to play a ton. It no longer seems to exist, and the alternatives I tried either had 'watch this ad' or 'pay for coins' to unlock either tools or drawing colours. HankyDoodle is a draw-and-guess game for iOS and Android. The main part I enjoyed working on was the file storage. I had to come up with a format for the drawing animations that had to be small but store enough information to be able to animate it at playback speeds. It also had to be practical to store and serve hundreds of thousands of them - right now I'm sitting at slightly less than 20,000 drawings. Currently, the drawing sizes are typically between 1 and 12kb. Drawings are recorded as a stream of operations that include each stroke's tool, colour, points and timing. The format (a small RLE/palette/varint container) and the renderer are one C core, which gets shared + linked multiple ways. This makes sure the rendering is byte-identical across all platforms (iOS, Android and WebAssembly). Unfortunately I did mess up some of the code used for flood fills and if I don't render the image at the same size the drawings come out slightly differently (for that reason I render all drawings at one size then resize after when I need thumbnails). Luckily I did build a version system into the drawings, so it's something future me (sucker) can deal with at some point. Drawings are stored in S3 and served via CloudFront. The backend is PHP and MySQL, but built in a way that I should be able to scale it out/replace it as needed. Although it was not originally planned, it makes a pretty neat demo that you can navigate to the website and playback drawings as well. https://hankydoodle.app/d/01M37AKQF6MCRRXCHB3YSAVBVG is an example of one of the more detailed drawings by someone with way more talent than me. The app has a 'word of the day' feature where users can submit their own artwork and that's an example of an extremely detailed one. Features of the game: - 1v1 async drawing and guessing. You draw a picture. Your opponent guesses when they get the chance. - A forever guess mode. If you don't want to draw you can just go in and guess drawings made by others. Drawings get 'released' into the forever guess pool once a user has guessed the drawing. - A word of the day where anyone can take a crack at drawing the word. - A showcase where the best drawings can be found. - Offline drawing, where you can draw while offline and without any sort of signup. - A 'doodlepedia' where you can try and draw every word. - An online portfolio of your drawings (such as https://hankydoodle.app/u/TP1N34 ). - Privacy mode, where your drawings are private and only the folks you draw with can see them. - Family mode where certain drawings and words get filtered completely out of your view. The app has an unobtrusive banner ad which can be removed via a $3.99USD/year subscription. I know people don't like subscriptions, but that was the best alternative I could come up with and still keep the app free to most while covering my costs. Happy to go deep on the format, the renderer, the fill, or the solo-dev tradeoffs.

projects.summary: Buy low in one city, travel, sell high. 15 days. Everyone plays the same market each day, and everyone ends up on the leaderboard. I'm a software engineer but also wanted to learn how to use Claude Code, so I challenged myself to make a similar game that was more family friendly. It's a web game designed to be played on a PC or phone. It's vanilla TypeScript with no framework. It's also the same game per day, allowing people to improve their scores and try to get a spot on the daily leaderboard. Click "Help" then "Walk me through my first trade" for a quick start. I'd love to get some players on there and get some feedback. I hope whoever plays it enjoys it.

projects.title: Show HN: Rename.Tools – Open-source bulk file renaming in the browser
projects.author: wayne8848
projects.summary: Hi HN, I built Rename.Tools after needing to rename a large batch of images. This is something I only do occasionally, so I couldn’t justify buying dedicated software for it. The free tools I tried didn’t quite fit my needs either. When I discovered the File System Access API, a browser-based tool felt like a natural fit: open a tab when I need it, rename my files locally, and close it when I’m done. No installation or account required. The main feature is a chain of rename rules. You can combine find-and-replace, regex, sequential numbering, case conversion, text insertion, cleanup, and custom JavaScript, then drag them into the order you want. A live preview shows the resulting filenames and detects conflicts before you apply changes. There are also a few features for more specific workflows: - Rename photos using EXIF metadata and music files using audio tags. - Filter files by name, extension, size, or modification time. - Save reusable presets and import, export, or share them through a URL. - Undo renaming operations or export undo scripts. - Match TV episodes through TMDb, using your own API key. Files are processed locally and aren’t uploaded. The optional TMDb lookup requires network access. Direct renaming requires a supported Chromium browser. You can also export Bash or PowerShell scripts to run locally, including from browsers that don’t support direct renaming. There’s a sample mode if you’d like to try it without selecting your own files. The project is free and open source. I’d be interested to hear how you handle occasional bulk renaming, which workflows this is missing, and whether anything feels confusing. Try it: https://rename.tools/en/app Source: https://github.com/chenz24/rename.tools
